papers.title: Entanglement in Collective Neutrino Oscillations on a Quantum Computer
papers.abstract: Simulations on a quantum computer have been propounded as a next-generation tool for studying neutrino flavour oscillations in dense environments like supernovae or neutron star mergers. However, quantum advantage hinges on the presence of quantum entanglement in the neutrino ensemble, and it has been argued that such entanglement becomes negligible in the limit of large neutrino number density. Here, we address this question by explicitly simulating the multiparticle dynamics of entangled neutrino ensembles with a varying number of particles, $N$, on both classical and quantum hardware, and comparing our results to those obtained with conventional ``mean-field'' methods based on Boltzmann-type kinetic equations. For simple toy systems, we demonstrate both analytically and numerically that, indeed, the predictions of full multiparticle simulations agree with those of mean-field methods in the large-$N$ limit. Along the way, we develop novel algorithms for the efficient simulation of entangled neutrino gases on both classical and quantum hardware. We then discuss physical situations in which an entangled neutrino system \emph{cannot} be described through mean-field dynamics alone and quantum entanglement therefore becomes phenomenologically relevant. We comment on the conditions under which these scenarios may be realized in supernova cores or neutron star mergers.
papers.reason: Simulates multiparticle quantum entanglement in collective neutrino oscillations on classical and quantum hardware, directly matching the reader's interest in supernova neutrino physics. [favorite author: Joachim Kopp]

summary.tldr: Evaluates the emergence of mean-field QKEs from entangled multi-neutrino systems and identifies physical regimes where quantum entanglement remains phenomenologically relevant in dense environments.
summary.novel_idea: Combines analytic proofs of mean-field QKE recovery at large $N$ with quantum circuits run on IBM Kingston (Heron R2) hardware and classical tensor/spin simulations up to $N = 2.6 \times 10^6$. It introduces concrete astrophysical counterexamples to the conventional 'irrelevant entanglement' paradigm, such as spatial neutrino streams with overlapping wavepackets ($\sim 10^{-12}\text{ cm}$) or multi-encounter scattering geometries.

summary.caveats: The spatial stream and multi-encounter models rely on simplified toy geometries; the actual extent of wavepacket delocalization under realistic core-collapse supernova conditions (e.g., via Landau levels) remains unquantified.

papers.title: Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities
papers.abstract: The gallium anomaly, a 20% deficit in the measured $\nu_e$ captures on $^{71}$Ga, remains unexplained. A recent work [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131805 (2026), arXiv:2512.20560] has proposed a solution based on the breakdown of the factorization of lepton and nuclear wavefunctions that underlies the prediction of the cross section, combined with ad hoc Gamow-Teller nuclear transition densities. We test this proposed solution with transition densities calculated within the nuclear shell model (NSM), normalized to the $^{71}$Ge electron-capture half-life and convolved with Dirac-Hartree-Fock-Slater electron wavefunctions. We explore several NSM interactions, bare and effective Gamow-Teller operators, as well as the impact of the valence space. In all cases, we obtain remarkably consistent NSM transition densities. Our factorized and nonfactorized cross sections agree, remaining 20% higher than the measured value. In addition, we use NSM single-nucleon transition densities as ansatz and find that solving the anomaly requires fine-tuned densities, with percent-level cancellations and an overall scale orders of magnitude larger than the calculated NSM ones. We conclude that the gallium anomaly is not solved when using realistic nuclear transition densities.
papers.reason: Tests the proposed nuclear transition density solution to the Gallium anomaly using the nuclear shell model and realistically constrained wavefunctions, directly addressing low-energy neutrino cross-section anomalies.

summary.tldr: Proves via nuclear shell model calculations that non-factorization of lepton and nuclear wavefunctions cannot resolve the Gallium anomaly, as realistic transition densities yield factorized and non-factorized cross sections agreeing within 1%.
summary.novel_idea: Rigorously evaluates a recent proposal claiming the Gallium anomaly is solved by breaking lepton-nuclear factorization using ad hoc nuclear transition densities. By calculating realistic Gamow-Teller (GT) transition densities within the Nuclear Shell Model (NSM) convolved with Dirac-Hartree-Fock-Slater electron wavefunctions, the authors demonstrate that ad hoc density fits require unphysical multi-order-of-magnitude scale modifications and extreme fine-tuning.
summary.method: Computes GT transition densities $C(r)$ for $^{71}\text{Ga}(\nu_e,e^-)^{71}\text{Ge}$ and $^{71}\text{Ge}$ electron capture across 9 NSM setups (JUN45, GCN2850, RG.PROLATE, JJ4BB, and LNPS interactions in $pf$ and $0g_{9/2}$ spaces, with bare and effective GT operators). Convolves $C(r)$ with relativistic bound and continuum electron wavefunctions $g_\kappa(r), f_\kappa(r)$ solved via RADIAL. Normalizes total strength using the measured $^{71}\text{Ge}$ EC half-life.
key_results: Calculated NSM radial GT transition densities $C(r)$ are remarkably robust across all 9 nuclear Hamiltonians, valence spaces, and GT operators.

Non-factorized cross sections for $^{51}\text{Cr}$ and $^{37}\text{Ar}$ sources match detailed-balance factorized cross sections within 1%, leaving a persistent $\sim 20\%$ deficit (ratio $\sigma_{\text{exp}}/\sigma_{\text{th}} \approx 0.83$).
Ad hoc transition densities that 'solve' the anomaly require overall radial scales $100-1000\times$ larger than NSM and severe percent-level cancellations between positive and negative lobes.
Single-particle orbital ansatz fits require density coefficients $\sim 3000\times$ larger than shell-model predictions to reproduce experimental capture rates.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts research on low-energy neutrino-nucleus cross sections, Gamow-Teller matrix elements, and the Gallium anomaly. It rules out nuclear wavefunction non-factorization as a solution, firmly refocusing the anomaly on experimental systematics or BSM physics (sterile neutrinos).
summary.caveats: Shell model calculations were restricted to valence spaces ($pf$ and $0g_{9/2}$); ab initio VS-IMSRG calculations with explicit two-body currents remain a desirable future check.

papers.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
papers.abstract: Neutrino-antineutrino annihilation above black-hole accretion discs is shaped both by general-relativistic transport and by neutrino flavour conversion. Whether these effects can be treated independently depends on how gravity weights the different flavour populations. We investigate this interplay using backward ray tracing in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, combined with an exact angular-moment formulation of the annihilation kernel that we validate against the analytic spherical solution and published disc calculations. We first establish that flavour-conversion corrections are independent of the spacetime geometry when conversion is uniform and the initial heavy-lepton neutrino emission is negligible. For uniform conversion, this separability remains approximately valid when the flavour-dependent emitting regions overlap: compared with the same discs in flat space, moving with the same local velocities, gravity enhances the deposited energy by factors of 1.4-5, while changing the relative conversion effect by no more than 6% for most temperature profiles considered; conversion that varies across the disc raises this to 22% around a rapidly spinning hole. A qualitatively different regime emerges when heavy-lepton neutrinos originate from an inner ring separated from the electron-flavour emitting regions. Relativistic bending and energy shifts preferentially enhance annihilations involving inner-ring neutrinos, producing relativistic conversion factors up to 2.4 times the flat-space ones. In one configuration, flavour equipartition reduces the deposition by 54% in flat space but increases it by 11% in Kerr spacetime. These results identify the spatial arrangement of flavour-dependent neutrinospheres as a key determinant, in the models considered, of whether flavour conversion and relativistic transport can be treated separately.
papers.reason: Calculates neutrino-antineutrino annihilation in curved spacetime combined with flavour conversion, perfectly matching core interests in supernova and astrophysical neutrino transport.

summary.tldr: Shows that GR light bending around black holes preferentially enhances $\nu\bar{\nu}\to e^+e^-$ annihilation involving inner-ring heavy-lepton neutrinos, altering flat-space flavor conversion factors by up to 2.4x and reversing net conversion effects.
summary.novel_idea: Establishes an exact separability theorem for neutrino annihilation when initial heavy-lepton emission is negligible, and shows how spatial segregation between flavor-dependent neutrinospheres breaks flat-space conversion factorizations in GR. It identifies a mechanism where GR light bending amplifies annihilations involving inner-ring neutrinos over outer-disc pairs by a factor of 3.
summary.method: Uses backward ray tracing in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes combined with an exact angular-moment expansion (rank 0, 1, 2) of redshifted energy moments without moment closures (implemented in ANNIHILUS). Evaluates local rates and deposited Killing energy $\dot{E}_\infty$ across thin Keplerian discs under parametrized linear flavor conversion maps.
key_results: Proves exact separability ($\delta = 0$): for uniform conversion and zero initial $\nu_x$ emission, the conversion ratio $\mathcal{R}$ is strictly independent of spacetime geometry and emission profiles.

For overlapping flavor neutrinospheres, GR enhances net deposition by factors of $1.4-5\times$, while changing uniform conversion factors by $\le 6\%$ (up to $22\%$ for non-uniform conversion at $a=0.99$).

For spatially segregated neutrinospheres (inner $\nu_x$ ring, outer $
u_e$ disc), GR alters flat-space conversion factors by up to $141\%$ ($2.4\times$).
Demonstrates sign reversal of flavor conversion: flavor equipartition reduces energy deposition by $54\%$ in flat space, but increases it by $11\%$ in Kerr spacetime ($a=0.99$).
summary.why_it_matters: Crucial for neutrino annihilation and transport in black-hole accretion discs and post-merger environments, demonstrating that flavor conversion and relativistic transport cannot be factorized when neutrinospheres are spatially segregated.
summary.caveats: Flavor conversion is parametrized via linear emission maps rather than dynamically solving collective quantum kinetic equations along geodesics, and free streaming without reabsorption is assumed.

papers.title: The ATAR, a dense and compact vertex detector for the PIONEER experiment
papers.abstract: PIONEER is an approved experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institut (PSI) in Villigen, Switzerland that aims to measure the charged-pion branching ratio to electrons vs. muons with an accuracy of 0.01%. This is an order of magnitude improvement in precision compared to its predecessors and approaches the accuracy of the standard model prediction. The key elements of PIONEER are a high resolution calorimeter built concentrically around the high granularity active target (ATAR). The ATAR is composed of a stack of 48 low gain avalanche strip detectors (LGADs) to stop the beam pions and provide detailed information of the event topology. This will include precise timing (in the order of 200ps), spatial information (to an accuracy of about 60 micro meter) and pulse height information with a high dynamic range to separate pion stops from muons and MIPs. To avoid affecting the energy measurement of the positrons, the readout electronics is placed outside the acceptance angle of the calorimeter. It is composed of a fast amplifier and a fast sampling chip digitizing the LGAD wave form for real time analysis. The paper describes the PIONEER-experiment with focus on the ATAR and its readout. The status of the development and activities in 2026 will be reported.
papers.reason: Details the ATAR active target of the PIONEER experiment measuring charged-pion branching ratios with LGADs, squarely in the core experimental neutrino/stopped-pion domain.

summary.tldr: Presents the design and performance requirements of ATAR, a 48-layer LGAD active target for the PIONEER experiment to measure $R^{\pi}_{e/\mu}$ to 0.01% precision.
summary.novel_idea: Details the Active Target (ATAR) for the PIONEER experiment at PSI, combining a 48-layer stack of thin ($120\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) trench-isolated LGAD strip sensors with off-axis fast waveform digitization to achieve 2 ns double-pulse pair separation and sub-200 ps timing in a 300 kHz pion beam environment.
summary.method: Constructs ATAR using $2\times 2\text{ cm}^2$ trench-isolated LGAD microstrips ($200\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ pitch) rotated $90^\circ$ layer-to-layer. Signals travel via 15 cm flex cables outside the calorimeter acceptance to FAST3 amplifier ASICs, digitized by HD-SoC or Sampic chips. Performs topological and pulse-shape rejection of the $\pi\to\mu\to e$ decay chain.
key_results: Achieves timing resolution of $\sim 200\text{ ps}$ and pulse-pair separation down to $2\text{ ns}$ in a single strip channel.
Pulse-height digitizations cleanly distinguish $14\text{ MeV}$ pion stops, $4.1\text{ MeV}$ decay muons, and MIP positrons.
Timing selection suppresses $\pi\to\mu\to e$ background by a factor of 160 while retaining $60\%$ of $\pi\to e$ events.
Combined topological and per-hit energy deposit analysis yields a factor 500 tail rejection while maintaining $50\%$ signal efficiency.
Constructed the ATAR 8 prototype stack (8-10 layers) for a PSI piM1 test beam run in late 2026.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant to precision tests of lepton flavor universality ($R^{\pi}_{e/\mu}$) and CKM unitarity ($|V_{ud}|$ via pion beta decay), detailing the vertex detector technology required to suppress systematic tail fractions.
summary.caveats: LGAD gain suppression under dense energy deposits (stopping muons/pions) requires ongoing calibration; final digitization chip selection between HD-SoC and Sampic remains to be finalized.

papers.title: Features of Non-Local Quantum Correlations in Nuclei
papers.abstract: Classical simulation of quantum many-body systems is challenged by the combined effects of entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic). Non-local magic, $M^{\mathrm{NL}}_\alpha$, quantifies the component of non-stabilizerness that cannot be removed by local unitary transformations and provides a measure of quantum complexity beyond entanglement alone. It is bounded from below by the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum, ${F}_A$. We calculate stabilizer R\'enyi entropies, non-local magic, entanglement-spectrum antiflatness, and entanglement entropy in shell-model ground states of more than 260 even-even, odd-even, and odd-odd nuclei, using a bipartition into proton and neutron sectors. We find that the previously established bound $4{F}_A\leq{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}}$ holds for every nucleus studied and approaches saturation in the limit of separable states. Odd-odd nuclei exhibit markedly different patterns of entanglement and magic compared with even-even and odd-even systems, revealing distinctive signatures of proton-neutron quantum correlations and providing new insight into the complexity generated by nuclear interactions.
papers.reason: Calculates non-local magic, entanglement entropy, and stabilizer Rényi entropies in shell-model ground states across over 260 nuclei, providing deep insight into nuclear many-body quantum complexity. [favorite author: Rocco]

summary.tldr: Evaluates non-local magic and entanglement spectrum antiflatness across 260+ nuclei, proving the bound $4\mathcal{F}_A \le \mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}}$ and uncovering distinct quantum complexity signatures in odd-odd nuclei.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the first systematic calculation of non-local non-stabilizerness (magic, $\mathcal{M}^{\text{NL}}_{\text{lin}}$) and entanglement-spectrum antiflatness ($\mathcal{F}_A$) in nuclear shell-model ground states across $>260$ nuclei using a proton-neutron bipartition. Discovers that odd-odd nuclei exhibit quantum complexity structures distinctly different from even-even and odd-even systems.
summary.method: Solves nuclear shell-model ground states using BIGSTICK with Cohen-Kurath ($p$), USDB ($sd$), GXPF1A ($pf$), and JUN45 ($pf_{5/2}g$) interactions. Maps nucleonic orbital occupations to 6-44 qubits via Jordan-Wigner transform. Computes proton-neutron entanglement entropy $S$, antiflatness $\mathcal{F}_A = \text{Tr}(\rho_A^2) - \text{Tr}(\rho_A^3)$, total SRE $\mathcal{M}_2$, and non-local SRE $\mathcal{M}^{\text{NL}}_2$ using auxiliary Schmidt states.
key_results: Confirms the lower bound $4\mathcal{F}_A \le \mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}}$ across all $>260$ calculated nuclei, with saturation approaching near separable states.

Even-even and odd-even nuclei trace a characteristic 'boomerang' trajectory in $\mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}}$ vs $4\mathcal{F}_A$, whereas odd-odd nuclei exhibit low antiflatness ($4\mathcal{F}_A \le 0.1$) despite high non-local magic.

Total non-stabilizerness per qubit is roughly constant across shells ($\mathcal{M}_2/N_q \approx 0.16-0.17$), peaking in strongly deformed nuclei such as $^{24}\text{Mg}$ ($\mathcal{M}_2/N_q \approx 0.44$).
Non-stabilizerness acts as an indicator of shell closures (dropping at $N=28, 40$), whereas antiflatness increases when approaching shell closures.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides quantitative measures of quantum complexity and non-stabilizerness in nuclear wavefunctions, informing the classical computational cost (tensor networks vs. quantum algorithms) for nuclear structure and proton-neutron correlations.
summary.caveats: Calculations rely on shell-model valence spaces and effective two-body Hamiltonians without explicit three-nucleon forces or continuum couplings; orbital occupation qubit mappings depend on single-particle basis choices.

papers.title: Exact and hybrid neutrino oscillation probabilities via the evolution operator
papers.abstract: We revisit the three-flavor neutrino oscillations in constant-density matter using the evolution matrix expressed in terms of the Lagrange-Sylvester interpolation. Taking advantage of Vieta's formulas for the Hamiltonian of the system, we derive exact closed expressions for the oscillation probabilities $P_{ee}$, $P_{\mu e}$, and $P_{\mu\tau}$, which are concise and simple, and structurally identical to their vacuum counterparts. The CP-violation contribution, proportional to the Jarlskog invariant $\mathcal{J}$, appears as a single, clearly separated term. Our approach does not require introducing neutrino mixing in the medium and avoids using a matter-dependent CP-violation phase, facilitating the separation of genuine CP violation from that induced by matter effects. We explicitly verify that, in the limit $V \to 0$, our expressions for the flavor transition probabilities reduce to the well-known vacuum formulas. The exact structure of the probabilities is preserved if the exact, not very enlightening, trigonometric eigenvalues are replaced by approximate expressions in radicals. We illustrate this hybrid approach with eigenvalues obtained from two successive rotations of the Hamiltonian. For an experiment like DUNE, the hybrid probability values match those of the exact probabilities within absolute errors of about $2\times 10^{-6}$ in all channels and relative errors less than $0.01 \%$ for $P_{ee}$, $P_{\mu e}$, and $P_{\mu\tau}$.
papers.reason: Derives exact and hybrid closed-form expressions for three-flavor neutrino oscillation probabilities in matter using Lagrange-Sylvester interpolation, specifically highlighting applications for DUNE.

summary.tldr: Exact closed-form expressions for three-flavor neutrino oscillation probabilities in constant-density matter are derived via the evolution operator and Vieta's formulas, yielding a high-accuracy hybrid approximation for DUNE.
summary.novel_idea: By utilizing Lagrange-Sylvester interpolation on the flavor-basis evolution operator and Vieta's traces, the authors avoid introducing matter-dependent mixing angles and non-standard CP phases. The resulting exact probability formulas are structurally identical to vacuum expressions, neatly separating genuine CP violation (proportional to the Jarlskog invariant) from matter-induced effects.
summary.method: The Schrödinger equation for flavor evolution in a constant-density medium (symmetric potential) is solved via the evolution operator matrix components. The Cayley-Hamilton theorem and Vieta's formulas for the cubic Hamiltonian eigenvalues are applied. A hybrid approach replaces the cumbersome trigonometric eigenvalues with approximate ones derived from two successive Hamiltonian rotations (1-3 and 1-2 planes).
key_results: For a DUNE-like setup, the hybrid probabilities match exact probabilities with absolute errors of $\sim 2 \times 10^{-6}$ and relative errors under $0.01\%$ across all channels.
Absolute errors of the hybrid approach are at least two orders of magnitude smaller than standard zeroth-order double-rotation approximations using the same eigenvalues.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to long-baseline oscillation systematics (DUNE) and interaction/propagation modeling workflows, offering clean analytical control over matter-induced CP violation without resorting to uncontrolled series expansions.
summary.caveats: Restricted strictly to constant-density media (or piecewise constant profiles); does not solve arbitrary position-dependent density profiles analytically.

papers.title: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos
papers.reason: Studies flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions over cosmological distances using high-energy astrophysical neutrinos from blazars and IceCube data.

summary.tldr: Flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions inside the TXS 0506+056 blazar spike alter neutrino propagation through MSW potentials and scattering attenuation, relaxing IceCube limits by up to four orders of magnitude.
summary.novel_idea: Combines flavor-dependent coherent forward scattering (MSW potentials) and incoherent scattering attenuation over cosmological distances from a dense DM spike. Discovers an 'eigenstate-isolation' regime at large potentials where only the interacting flavor's eigenstate is attenuated, producing a survival plateau.
summary.method: Models adiabatic neutrino propagation from the emission radius inside the TXS 0506+056 SMBH dark matter spike ($R_{	ext{em}} = 0.023$ pc) through the Galactic halo to Earth. Computes medium-modified PMNS mixing matrices and evaluates flavor composition changes and flux attenuation against IceCube 68% and 95% C.L. boundaries.
key_results: Local Galactic DM density constraints require the effective potential parameter $A_\alpha \lesssim 10^{-30}\text{ cm}^3$ to prevent distortion of vacuum PMNS mixing at 100 TeV.
For $A \ll 10^{-38}\text{ cm}^3$, standard attenuation limits give $\sigma_{\nu\chi}/m_\chi \lesssim 10^{-28}\text{ cm}^2/\text{GeV}$.

For $A \gg 10^{-36}\text{ cm}^3$, eigenstate isolation confines the interacting flavor to a single matter eigenstate, creating a survival plateau that relaxes $90\%$ flux attenuation bounds up to $\sim 5.6 \times 10^{-25}\text{ cm}^2/\text{GeV}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Connects low-energy/astrophysical BSM physics (neutrino-dark matter interactions, vector portal models) with high-energy IceCube astrophysical neutrino flavor data and MSW medium propagation.
summary.caveats: Assumes a specific $\gamma_{\text{sp}} = 7/3$ DM spike profile around TXS 0506+056 and neglects energy-redistribution/regeneration from forward scattering via light mediators.

papers.title: New Neutron Polarizabilities from Deuterium Compton Scattering at HI$\gamma$S
papers.abstract: Elastic and inelastic Compton-scattering cross sections of the deuteron were measured at HI$\gamma$S using a circularly polarized, quasi-monoenergetic $\gamma$-ray beam (61.0 MeV). Scattered $\gamma$ rays from a liquid deuterium target were detected at $55^\circ$, $115^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. High-resolution NaI(Tl) detectors at backward angles enabled separation of elastic and inelastic events. A $\chi$EFT analysis of the data yields new neutron scalar polarizabilities, $\alpha^n_{E1} = 12.25 \pm 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \pm 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \pm 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ and $\beta^n_{M1} = 2.95 \mp 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \mp 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \mp 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ (in units of $10^{-4} \mathrm{fm}^3$) reducing statistical uncertainties by 12 %.
papers.reason: Uses chiral EFT and deuterium Compton scattering to extract neutron scalar polarizabilities, highly relevant for nucleon structure and electroweak interactions.

summary.tldr: New elastic and inelastic deuteron Compton-scattering cross sections measured at 61 MeV at HI$\gamma$S yield updated neutron scalar polarizabilities with a 12% reduction in statistical uncertainty.
summary.novel_idea: Presents high-precision separation of elastic and inelastic (deuteron breakup) Compton scattering cross sections at backward angles using large-volume NaI(Tl) detectors, providing the first experimental benchmark for recent $\chi$EFT calculations of the inelastic channel below 100 MeV.
summary.method: Utilized a circularly polarized, quasi-monoenergetic 61.0 MeV $\gamma$-ray beam from the HI$\gamma$S facility incident on a liquid deuterium target. Scattered photons were detected at $55^\circ$, $115^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. Net yields were analyzed within the chiral effective field theory ($\chi$EFT) framework constrained by the Baldin Sum Rule (BSR).
key_results: Extracted new neutron scalar polarizabilities: $\alpha^n_{E1} = 12.25 \pm 1.1\text{(stat)} \pm 0.3\text{(BSR)} \pm 0.8\text{(th)}$ and $\beta^n_{M1} = 2.95 \mp 1.1\text{(stat)} \mp 0.3\text{(BSR)} \mp 0.8\text{(th)}$ in units of $10^{-4}\text{ fm}^3$.
Inclusion of the new data in the world dataset reduces statistical uncertainties of isoscalar polarizabilities by $16.7\%$.
Total neutron polarizability statistical uncertainty is reduced by $12\%$ compared to previous extractions.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides vital nucleon-structure inputs (axial/vector form factors and electromagnetic responses) and low-energy precision benchmarks that interface with nuclear EFT calculations relevant to electroweak neutrino-nucleus scattering.
summary.caveats: Inelastic and elastic contributions could not be reliably separated at the forward $55^\circ$ angle and were reported only as a combined cross section.

papers.title: The PICO-40L detector
papers.abstract: The PICO collaboration has designed and constructed a novel bubble chamber to search for evidence of Weakly Interacting Massive Particles, a leading dark matter candidate. The PICO-40L detector is the successor to PICO-60, and uses a fully redesigned system for pressurization of the active volume after a bubble nucleation event. Pressure in PICO-40L is transferred to the target fluid through a set of two nested synthetic quartz vessels connected by bellows below the active volume. This is in contrast to the design of earlier detectors in which the pressure was transferred through a buffer fluid atop the target fluid, within a single synthetic quartz vessel connected to a bellows above the active volume. Removing the buffer fluid removes the potential for backgrounds arising from the interface between the two fluids, and moving the bellows below the target fluid suppresses potential backgrounds from particulates originating from the bellows. The newly designed detector concept of PICO-40L is referred to as the Right-Side-Up (RSU) design and requires a dedicated thermal system to keep the lower region of the detector cold while the upper region is stably superheated. The main goal of PICO-40L is to establish the performance characteristics of the RSU detector concept, which will inform the operating configuration of the final generation PICO dark matter detector, PICO-500, which is currently under construction at SNOLAB. This paper reviews the design, installation, and performance of the PICO-40L detector.
papers.reason: Presents the design and performance of the PICO-40L bubble chamber for dark matter searches, relevant to low-background noble liquid and bubble chamber detector technologies. [favorite author: Richard Hill]

summary.tldr: PICO-40L is a novel Right-Side-Up (RSU) bubble chamber designed to eliminate buffer-fluid and bellows-particulate backgrounds for dark matter searches, serving as a prototype for PICO-500.
summary.novel_idea: Introduces the Right-Side-Up (RSU) design where pressure is transferred via two nested synthetic quartz vessels connected to a bellows *below* the active volume, completely removing the traditional buffer fluid interface and isolating bellows-particulate backgrounds.
summary.method: Constructed a two-vessel quartz assembly containing a $\text{C}_3\text{F}_8$ target, housed inside a pressure vessel filled with mineral oil. Integrated a dedicated thermal system (using a bottom coil chiller and HDPE insulation) to maintain a cold sub-cooled region in the lower bellows and a stably superheated active volume above. Deployed 12 piezoelectric acoustic transducers, four optical cameras, and fast pressure accumulators.
key_results: Achieved a measured radon emanation rate of $20.1 \pm 2.0$ atoms/day of $^{222}\text{Rn}$ dominated by the nitrile O-ring seal.

Successfully demonstrated stable operation and background discrimination capabilities (acoustic, optical stereo reconstruction, and Dytran fast pressure growth) during $^{252}\text{Cf}$ calibration and commissioning runs at SNOLAB.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to low-background experimental hardware and dark matter direct detection techniques, validating background suppression strategies critical for future low-energy noble-gas/fluorine detectors.
summary.caveats: Commissioning data indicated that operating setpoints near $13^\circ\text{C}$ and $189.6\text{ kPa}$ caused a slightly elevated rate of background boiling while investigating cold-region stability.

papers.title: Opening up derivative baryon-number-violating operators
papers.abstract: Baryon number violation is our most sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model, typically encoded in higher-dimensional effective operators. Operators involving derivatives are often ignored in phenomenological analyses since they are generically suppressed compared to non-derivative operators. We systematically construct tree-level UV completions of derivative baryon-number-violating operators up to mass dimension 12 in the Standard Model effective field theory (extended by right-handed neutrinos) and show that derivative operators need not be suppressed. Our public code can be used to UV-complete other derivative operators.
papers.reason: Systematically constructs tree-level UV completions of derivative baryon-number-violating operators in SMEFT up to mass dimension 12, directly addressing effective field theory matching.

summary.tldr: A systematic construction of tree-level UV completions for derivative baryon-number-violating (BNV) operators up to mass dimension 12 reveals that derivative BNV operators need not be suppressed.
summary.novel_idea: Demonstrates that derivative BNV operators are not generically suppressed relative to non-derivative ones. Specifically identifies non-trivial UV completions (via heavy scalars and fermions) where odd-derivative operators lack non-derivative counterparts due to Lorentz/gauge structure, or where multi-derivative operators become the leading contribution because lower-order non-derivative terms vanish due to Higgs field antisymmetry.
summary.method: Generated simplified BNV operators up to dimension 12 using Sym2Int and systematically matched them against tree-level topologies using scalar and fermion mediators in SMEFT and $\nu$SMEFT (excluding gauge bosons). Developed public code and data repositories for UV-completing derivative operators.
key_results: Constructed over one million non-trivial tree-level UV completions for derivative BNV operators up to mass dimension 12.
Identified that non-trivial one-, two-, three-, and four-derivative operators first emerge at mass dimensions $d = 8$, $10$, $12$, and $14$, respectively.

Highlighted that Higgs-field antisymmetry forces certain non-derivative operators to vanish, making derivative insertions the leading term in the heavy-mass expansion without fine-tuned cancellations.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly touches SMEFT/LEFT matching, BNV operator bases, and effective field theory frameworks used for precision nucleon decay and beyond-the-Standard-Model phenomenology.
summary.caveats: Non-trivial UV completions guarantee operator dominance in the heavy-mass expansion only prior to considering loop-induced lower-dimensional operator regeneration, which must be checked model by model.

papers.title: Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$ from Chiral Perturbation Theory
papers.abstract: We construct effective operators for transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) distributions in Chiral Perturbation Theory. The operators constructed from pion and nucleon fields possess the main properties of the QCD operators, including multiplicatively renormalizable rapidity divergences. Extracting the leading rapidity divergence, we find the expression for the Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$ and at the low-energy normalization point, which is model-independent up to an additive constant. In this regime, the Collins-Soper kernel has a nearly constant behavior. We also find that at large $b$ it depends on the isospin channel and on the hadron type, although this dependence is numerically very small.
papers.reason: Constructs TMD effective operators in Chiral Perturbation Theory and derives the Collins-Soper kernel at large $b$, directly bridging low-energy EFT with QCD parton dynamics.

papers.title: An interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles
papers.abstract: We conjecture a novel interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles: $\theta^{}_{23} = \left(\theta^{}_{12} + \theta^{}_{13}\right)/2 + \pi/8$, which predicts $\theta^{}_{23} = 43.46^{+0.51^\circ}_{-0.52^\circ}$ with inputs of the latest JUNO and Daya Bay precision data. A simple ansatz is proposed to derive this phenomenologically favored and experimentally testable angle relation, and present a new expansion of the lepton flavor mixing matrix in powers of a single small parameter as a by-product.
papers.reason: Conjectures a novel analytical interrelation among the three neutrino mixing angles and proposes a new lepton mixing matrix expansion, highly relevant to global oscillation data.

papers.title: Magic Is in the Eye of the Measure
papers.abstract: Magic, or nonstabilizerness, is the quantum resource behind universal quantum computation. Its applications in high-energy and nuclear physics rely almost exclusively on the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE), although magic has no unique measure. For two qubits, we compare the SRE with three measures defined through optimizations over stabilizer states: the min- and max-relative entropies of magic and the logarithmic free robustness. We determine the maximal-magic states of all four measures, with exact proofs, and find that they depend on the measure. In the determination of the weak mixing angle from minimal magic in M{\o}ller scattering, the min-relative entropy gives an energy-dependent value that differs from that of the SRE, whereas the max-relative entropy and the logarithmic free robustness give $\sin^2\theta_W=1/4$ at all energies. We trace this difference to the non-analytic structure of the optimization-based measures. Physical conclusions drawn from extremizing magic can thus depend on the measure.
papers.reason: Compares measures of quantum nonstabilizerness (magic) and evaluates them in Møller scattering, connecting well to quantum information in scattering and precision observables.

papers.title: Chiral Response of QCD Topology across the Thermal Crossover
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel relation connecting the light-quark-mass derivative of the topological susceptibility in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) to the connected correlation between the squared topological charge and the integrated light-quark scalar density. This relation gives direct access to the chiral response of QCD topology---the local logarithmic light-quark-mass derivative of the susceptibility---from a single ensemble at fixed quark masses for each temperature, without additional simulations at shifted masses. Applying this relation to $(2+1)$-flavor lattice QCD at $m_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$ over temperatures ranging from well below to well above the chiral crossover, we find that the response rises rapidly through the crossover from approximately unity toward two. This evolution corresponds to a change from nearly linear to nearly quadratic dependence of the topological susceptibility on the light-quark mass. Using the chiral response as the exponent of a local power law in the light-quark mass, we determine its effective amplitude from the topological susceptibility. This amplitude exhibits a maximum near the crossover temperature, reflecting the competition between the decreasing topological susceptibility and the increasing chiral response. These results reveal a thermal reorganization of the quark-mass dependence of QCD topology beyond the suppression of topological fluctuations alone.
papers.reason: Explores the chiral response of QCD topology and light-quark-mass derivatives across the thermal crossover using lattice QCD, relevant to non-perturbative QCD inputs.

papers.title: Independent nuclear charge radius determinations: bound-electron $g$ factor versus muonic atom spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We present an alternative method to determine absolute nuclear charge radii competitively via the bound electron $g$ factor of H-like ions. The method is demonstrated for $^{118}$Sn by extracting its radius with a precision of 0.1%. This is the second most precise radius ever determined from an electronic system. We benchmark our result against a state-of-the-art value derived from the spectrum of muonic $^{118}$Sn. This comparison reveals a 3.2$\sigma$ tension, prompting a careful reexamination of the calculations and calling for additional measurements. Crucially, after decades, we now have two independent methods to measure absolute charge radii with similar precision.
authors: B. Ohayon (The Helen Diller Quantum Center
papers.reason: Extracts absolute nuclear charge radii from bound-electron g factors and compares with muonic atom spectroscopy, connecting directly to precision nuclear probes.

papers.abstract:

papers.title: Flat "Island of Stability" of Superheavy Nuclei
papers.abstract: We present the first systematic microscopic calculations of fission barrier heights for 292 even-even superheavy nuclei using the multidimensionally constrained relativistic mean field model with triaxial and octupole deformations treated simultaneously. The calculated barrier heights remain around 5 MeV in the vicinity of the predicted doubly magic nucleus ${}^{304}120$. This flat landscape contrasts with the conventional picture of mutually enhanced magicity and indicates that the proton shell closure at $Z=120$ and the neutron shell closure at $N=184$ do not reinforce but suppress each other. We introduce an $\alpha$-linked energy difference $\Delta_{\rm pn}$ to identify the mutually suppressed magicity caused by distinct proton and neutron density distributions. These results challenge the expected shell landscape of superheavy nuclei and may have a crucial impact on estimating survival probabilities in the synthesis of superheavy nuclei.
papers.reason: Performs microscopic calculations of fission barrier heights for superheavy nuclei near doubly magic ${}^{304}120$, providing important nuclear structure inputs.

papers.title: Renormalon-chain contributions to two-point correlators of nonlocal quark currents and light-meson distribution amplitudes
papers.abstract: In the framework of QCD sum rules, we study the endpoint slopes of the leading-twist distribution amplitudes in the large-$\beta_0$ approximation for the pion and the longitudinally polarized $\rho$ meson. To this end, we compute the two-point massless correlator of non-local composite vector quark currents with the gluon lines dressed by chains of one-loop fermion bubbles. This correlator depends on the Bjorken fraction $x$ associated with the composite current and, within the large-$\beta_0$ approximation, provides the dominant contribution in each order of perturbation theory. We derive an inequality for the second Gegenbauer moments of these distribution amplitudes that agrees with predictions from lattice QCD.
papers.reason: Studies endpoint slopes of leading-twist distribution amplitudes for pion and $ho$ mesons using renormalon-chain contributions and QCD sum rules, relevant for hadron structure.

papers.title: Stimulated Axion Decay around Primordial Black Holes and the Diffuse Radio Background
papers.abstract: We study stimulated axion decay in dense axion halos around primordial black holes (PBHs), assuming that both PBHs and axions contribute to dark matter. We construct the axion density profile by matching a hydrogenic soliton-like core dominated by the PBH potential to the $r^{-9/4}$ spike produced by secondary infall. We also impose an inner cutoff at the innermost stable circular orbit. We derive local Boltzmann equations for the number densities of photons and axions, including spontaneous and stimulated decay, inverse decay, photon escape, and axion filling. We solve these equations numerically and with a semi-analytic approximation. Stimulated emission occurs within an inner region where photon amplification overcomes escape. We calculate the photon emission from an individual PBH halo and integrate it over the population of PBHs throughout cosmic history. By requiring the resulting diffuse radio spectrum not to exceed the radio background measured by ARCADE~2, we derive upper bounds on the fraction of dark matter in PBHs. The bounds are strongest at intermediate PBH masses and apply over a wider mass range as the coupling between axions and photons increases.
papers.reason: Calculates stimulated axion decay in dense axion halos around primordial black holes and constrains them using radio background data.

papers.title: Roles of $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$ in the process $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$: a clean probe of the $K\bar K$ final-state interaction
papers.abstract: Based on the Belle measurement of $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$, we study the contributions of the light scalar mesons $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$, dynamically generated from the $S$-wave pseudoscalar meson--pseudoscalar meson interaction within the chiral unitary approach, to the threshold enhancement in the $K_S^0K_S^0$ invariant mass squared distribution, and examine the possible contribution of the intermediate $\Sigma(1620)$ resonance in the $pK_S^0$ subsystem. We first argue that the $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK_S^0K_S^0$ channel is a cleaner probe of the $K\bar K$ final-state interaction than the charged channel $\Lambda_c^+ \to pK^+K^-$, since the $\phi$ and $\Lambda^*$ contributions are forbidden and the $\Sigma(1620)$ and $\Sigma(1660)$ couple weakly to the $\bar{K}N$ channel. The threshold enhancement in the $K_S^0K_S^0$ invariant mass squared distribution is well described by the $S$-wave $K^0\bar K^0$ final-state interaction alone, with the $f_0(980)$ contribution dominating while that of $a_0(980)$ is small, supporting the interpretation of $f_0(980)$ as a $K\bar K$ hadronic molecular state. Future high-precision measurements by Belle~II and the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility will help test the roles of the $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$ and of the possible $\Sigma(1620)$ contribution in this process.
papers.reason: Examines $f_0(980)$ and $a_0(980)$ contributions and $K ar{K}$ final-state interactions in $\Lambda_c^+ 	o pK_S^0K_S^0$ decays using chiral unitary approaches.

papers.title: Relativistic analogue of the Kramers-Henneberger transformation and pair creation
papers.abstract: In analogy to the Kramers-Henneberger transformation in non-relativistic quantum mechanics, we propose and investigate a spinor transformation for the Dirac equation which allows us to transform space-time dependent vector potentials $A(t,x)\boldsymbol{e}$_x away. In the mass-less case, we exactly arrive at the free Dirac equation, while for massive Dirac fields, the transformation results in a non-trivial mass matrix containing space-time dependent phases. Special emphasis is placed on the phenomenon of fermion pair creation in the external field $A(t,x)\boldsymbol{e}_x$ where the spinor transformation allows us to conceptually disentangle the different contributions to pair creation. It can also be used to reformulate the WKB approach and the Riccati equation (which can be advantageous in certain cases) and to obtain additional insight into the mechanism of dynamically assisted pair creation.
papers.reason: Proposes a spinor transformation for the Dirac equation to study fermion pair creation in external fields, highly relevant to strong-field QED and neutrino-related scattering analogues.

papers.title: Soft-gluon effective coupling for massive quarks
papers.abstract: We present a generalisation of the soft-gluon physical coupling, defined in terms of the strength of soft radiation from a hard dipole, to massive hard emitters. We derive the relation between this coupling and the $\overline{\rm MS}$ coupling through two loops, encompassing all configurations in which both, one, or neither of the hard emitters are massive. We show that the presence of massive emitters introduces additional freedom in the definition of the physical coupling scheme, which we characterise at two-loop order. Our results provide new ingredients for precision QCD resummation in processes involving heavy quarks and for the development of higher-order parton-shower algorithms.
papers.reason: Derives soft-gluon physical couplings for massive quarks, which is moderately useful for heavy-quark and parton-shower QCD applications.

papers.title: A Phase-Transition Portal to Enhanced Dark Matter Annihilation
papers.abstract: We present a thermal dark matter (DM) scenario in which a phase transition after freeze-out changes both the DM spectrum and the dominant annihilation process, allowing an enhanced present day annihilation rate with suppressed direct detection. We realize this mechanism in a two-Higgs-doublet model extended by a complex scalar singlet, a Majorana fermion, and a heavier Dirac fermion. Before the transition, the Majorana state freezes out through $p$-wave annihilation into singlet scalars. The subsequent transition changes the dark fermion masses and mixing, enabling $s$-wave annihilation through a pseudoscalar portal. The surviving relic differs in mass and composition from the original state. We find relic compatible solutions with present day annihilation rates more than an order of magnitude above the canonical thermal value, without tuning to a mediator resonance, while satisfying direct detection bounds.
papers.reason: Presents a thermal dark matter model with a late-time phase transition altering annihilation rates, crossing over into phenomenology.

papers.title: Twist-3 and flavor-singlet contributions to $\gamma\gamma\to\pi^{0}\eta^{(\prime)}$ and $\eta^{(\prime)}\eta^{(\prime)}$ in $k_{T}$ factorization
papers.abstract: We study two-photon production of the pseudoscalar pairs $\pi^{0}\eta$, $\pi^{0}\eta^{\prime}$, $\eta\eta$, $\eta\eta^{\prime}$, and $\eta^{\prime}\eta^{\prime}$ at center-of-mass energies $2<Q<4\,\mathrm{GeV}$ in $k_{T}$ factorization, including the chirally enhanced twist-3 amplitudes and the two-gluon component of the $\eta^{(\prime)}$. The twist-3 amplitudes raise the hard cross sections by about an order of magnitude in all five channels. They bring $\eta\eta$ close to the Belle data, while $\pi^{0}\eta$ stays 3 to 5 times below and falls too slowly with energy. Varying the two-gluon distribution amplitude within its uncertainty changes the cross sections by about 2% in $\pi^{0}\eta$ and $\eta\eta$ but by up to 24% in the $\eta^{\prime}$ channels, making them its probe. The hard and handbag mechanisms each give nearly constant ratios $\sigma(\pi^{0}\eta)/\sigma(\pi^{0}\pi^{0})$ and $\sigma(\eta\eta)/\sigma(\pi^{0}\pi^{0})$, whereas below $3.2\,\mathrm{GeV}$ the measured $\pi^{0}\eta$ ratio lies above both predictions and the $\eta\eta$ ratio below them. Adding the handbag amplitude coherently, with its modulus fixed by the pion and kaon channels and its phase fitted, reproduces the $\pi^{0}\eta$ ratio up to $4\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the $\eta\eta$ ratio below $2.8\,\mathrm{GeV}$, and steepens $\sigma(\pi^{0}\eta)$ to a $Q^{-n}$ dependence with $n=9.7\pm1.6$, against the measured $10.5\pm1.2\pm0.5$. The energy dependence of the cross section ratios can thus be understood as the interference of two mechanisms of comparable size.
papers.reason: Studies twist-3 and flavor-singlet contributions to two-photon pseudoscalar pair production in $k_T$ factorization, touching on chiral perturbation and parton distributions.

papers.title: Baryon Number Susceptibilities of Hot and Dense Nuclear Matter in Relativistic Mean-Field Models
papers.abstract: We develop a fully analytical framework for calculating baryon number susceptibilities in relativistic mean-field (RMF) models of hot and dense nuclear matter at finite temperature and baryon chemical potential. The formalism is applied to representative nonlinear RMF parameterization sets to investigate the model dependence of baryon number fluctuations over a wide range of temperatures and baryon chemical potentials. All the considered RMF parameterizations reproduce the overall qualitative beam-energy dependence of the cumulant ratios. The observed skewness and kurtosis within the RMF models satisfy the experimental values. Specifically, the FSU-family parameterizations exhibit relatively small deviations from the measured heavy-ion observables i.e. cumulant ratios.
papers.reason: Computes baryon number susceptibilities and cumulant ratios in hot and dense nuclear matter using relativistic mean-field models, relevant for heavy-ion and dense matter EoS.

papers.title: Production of hidden-charm molecular candidates with hidden strangeness in $B_s^0$ decays
papers.abstract: We study the production of spin-one $D_{s0}^*(2317)\bar D_s^*$, $D_{s1}(2460)\bar D_s^*$, and $D_{s1}(2536)\bar D_s^*$ molecular candidates in $B_s^0$ decays with an accompanying $\eta$, providing a complementary probe of their structure and production mechanisms. The meson-loop rescattering amplitudes are constructed from factorized weak sources and heavy-hadron chiral interactions. Constituent couplings are estimated using threshold-dependent compositeness relations, and the associated input uncertainties are propagated to the predicted rates. Opposite-$C$-parity partner hypotheses are included with inherited benchmark parameters. We calculate the branching fractions for two relative signs. Over the cutoff range $2\leq\alpha\leq5$, the larger central branching fractions reach several $10^{-6}$ to several $10^{-5}$, suggesting potential accessibility in future experimental measurements.
papers.reason: Investigates molecular candidate production in $B_s^0$ decays via meson-loop rescattering and heavy-hadron chiral interactions.

papers.title: Restoration of rotational symmetry in light-front dynamics
papers.abstract: Solving the bound state problem in the framework of the light-front dynamics (with the state vector defined in the light-front plane t+z=0), one finds that after truncation - representing approximately the state vector by a finite number of the Fock components, the binding energies become to depend on projection of the angular momentum on the z-axes. This is so called violation of rotational symmetry in light-front dynamics. It is shown that the physical solution is the superposition of these states with some well defined coefficients. For a test, we also solve the Bethe-Salpeter equation and projecting its solution on the light-front, we find the wave functions which do not suffer from violation of the rotation invariance. Comparison with them of solution in the form of superposition shows that not only binding energies but also the wave functions themselves are described by the superpositions of the split states fairly well.
papers.reason: Addresses rotational symmetry violations in light-front dynamics by constructing physical superpositions, directly relevant to light-front wavefunction calculations.

papers.title: Spin Correlations in $t\bar{t}$ Production and Decay at the LHC in Perturbative QCD
papers.abstract: Among recent developments in top-quark physics at the LHC, the production of top-quark pairs near threshold has attracted considerable attention, partly due to tensions between data and theoretical predictions. We show that reliable predictions for threshold-sensitive observables, such as spin correlations and the differential distribution in the $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass, can be obtained in perturbation theory by retaining the first few powers of $\alpha_s/v$, where $v$ is the relative velocity of the top quarks. Applying this approach to reweight nominal Monte Carlo predictions for spin-sensitive observables, we find good agreement with data. We also discuss how threshold effects, including bound-state contributions, can be incorporated on an event-by-event basis into fully differential Monte Carlo event generators.
papers.topic: Spin Correlations in Top Pair Production
papers.reason: Analyzes threshold-sensitive spin correlations and differential distributions in $t\bar{t}$ production using perturbative QCD and velocity expansions.

papers.title: Nucleon-resonance contributions to the $p\bar{p}\to\eta_c\eta$ reaction
papers.abstract: Within an effective Lagrangian approach, we investigate the associated charmonium production reaction $p\bar{p}\to\eta_c\eta$ from threshold up to $\sqrt{s}=5.00\,\mathrm{GeV}$, incorporating intermediate contributions from the ground-state nucleon and the nucleon resonances $N(1535)$, $N(1650)$, $N(1895)$, and $N(1710)$. The effective resonance parameters are constrained by the BESIII measurement of the crossed decay $\eta_c\to p\bar{p}\eta$ for both the constructive (Solution C) and destructive (Solution D) radiative-interference solutions. Using these decay-constrained parameters, we predict the total and differential Born cross sections for the $p\bar{p}\to\eta_c\eta$ reaction. We show that coherent resonance exchanges dominate the near-threshold production dynamics and significantly enhance the total cross section compared to the pure nucleon-exchange contribution, which suffers from a strong dynamical cancellation. As the collision energy increases, the rapidly growing nucleon contribution progressively dilutes the resonance terms, reducing the relative difference between the total cross sections for Solutions C and D. Furthermore, while the pure nucleon-exchange amplitude exhibits an exact dynamical zero at $\theta=90^\circ$ due to the pseudoscalar coupling structure, resonance exchanges fill this node in the predicted angular distributions, providing an observable test of the underlying exchange mechanisms. These predictions can be tested in future antiproton annihilation experiments at $\bar{\mathrm{P}}\mathrm{ANDA}$.
papers.reason: Investigates nucleon-resonance contributions to $p\bar{p} \to \eta_c \eta$ reactions using effective Lagrangians constrained by radiative-interference data.

papers.title: Effect of collective nuclear vibrations on initial anisotropies in central Pb+Pb collisions: A comparative study in Glauber and Trento models
papers.abstract: We perform a comparison of the Glauber and Trento model predictions for the initial state azimuthal anisotropies $\epsilon_{2,3}\{2\}$ in central Pb+Pb collisions at the LHC energies. We incorporate the quantum collective effects in $^{208}$Pb by sampling nucleon positions with filterings in the quadrupole and octupole moments. We use the data-driven filters adjusted to reproduce the mean squared quadrupole and octupole moments extracted from the experimental strength functions. We find that the collective effects reduce considerably the $\epsilon_2\{2\}/\epsilon_3\{2\}$ ratio. The reduction is more pronounced in the Trento model. We obtain $\epsilon_2\{2\}/\epsilon_3\{2\}\approx 0.75\div 0.79(0.68\div 0.71)$ in the Glauber(Trento) models. These values allow to resolve the $v_2$-to-$v_3$ puzzle.
papers.reason: Studies the impact of collective quadrupole and octupole nuclear vibrations in ${}^{208}\text{Pb}$ on initial anisotropies in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.
papers.reason: Studies flow harmonics and Pearson response correlations in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions using an AI-accelerated hydrodynamic model.

papers.title: Uncovering TeV-scale dark matter with Z-fusion at a muon collider
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the advantage of the $Z$-boson fusion channel at a high-energy, high-luminosity muon collider in eliciting signals of a TeV-scale scalar dark matter (DM) particle. The utility of such a set-up lies in (a)the attainability of high centre-of-mass energy ($\approx 10 ~\rm TeV$), (b)the likely availability of large integrated luminosity ($\gtrsim 10~ab^{-1}$), and (c)the facility for efficient detection of very forward tagged muons. Our analysis is based on the process $\mu^+ \mu^- \rightarrow \mu^+ \mu^-$ + missing energy, driven by $Z$-fusion. We present the results in the context of (i) a scenario characterised by dimension-6 effective couplings, and (ii) an inert doublet model. After filtering each scenario through its associated constraints, we find that it is possible to achieve a signal significance of about 6.7$\sigma$ in case (i) and about 5.5$\sigma$ in case (ii), for DM particle masses $\approx$ 1 TeV and an integrated luminosity of $10 ~ ab^{-1}$.
papers.topic: Z-Fusion Dark Matter at Muon Collider
papers.reason: Demonstrates the utility of the $Z$-boson fusion channel at a high-energy muon collider for detecting TeV-scale scalar dark matter.

papers.title: Emergence and polymer physics of the center-vortex network: Confronting SU(4) lattice Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: The geometric organization and statistical properties of center-vortex networks provide a window into the infrared dynamics underlying confinement in Yang-Mills theory. Motivated by this connection, we investigate new consequences of a previously proposed confinement mechanism based on physically equivalent elementary Cartan fluxes. We show that, in the percolating phase, these fluxes dynamically reorganize into center-charge sectors whose dominant vortex tensions satisfy a Casimir scaling law, similar to that observed for confining string tensions. We then confront this result with the first nontrivial Yang-Mills case: the doubly charged vortex chains recently observed in SU(4) lattice simulations. To extract the parameters needed to connect the lattice ensemble with the effective description, we characterize how center-vortex chains grow and bend in SU(3) and SU(4) using polymer-inspired techniques not previously applied to center vortices. We find good quantitative agreement for the SU(4) doubly charged sector, providing further evidence for the proposed mechanism.
papers.reason: Investigates center-vortex networks and polymer physics in SU(4) lattice Yang-Mills theory, touching on confinement mechanisms relevant to non-perturbative QCD.

papers.title: Observing Transverse Momentum Broadening from TEECs in Heavy Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: We study the azimuthal dependence of transverse energy-energy correlators (TEECs) in dijet events in heavy-ion collisions. In the back-to-back region this observable resolves the energy flow around $\phi=\pi$ and is sensitive to medium-induced momentum broadening and the response of the medium. To isolate final-state effects, we consider a quark-antiquark pair produced in a colour-singlet hard process and propagating through a homogeneous background medium. Starting from the vacuum TMD factorization formula, we combine NLL$'$ resummation with medium modifications at first order in the strong coupling. For the parameters studied, (classical) momentum broadening lowers the back-to-back peak and leaves the distribution elsewhere nearly unchanged, while radiative corrections significantly suppress the peak further and enhance larger angular decorrelations. We additionally include the medium response sourced by each jet, as a mean energy flow. This spreads the deposited energy over the whole azimuth, so that the contribution to the TEEC varies slowly across the back-to-back region, is small at the peak and grows toward larger angles.
papers.reason: Analyzes transverse energy-energy correlators in heavy-ion collisions, touching upon hadronization and parton shower concepts in a heavy-ion context.

papers.title: GeoRead: Geometry-Aware Transformer for Continuous AC-LGAD Readout Reconstruction
papers.abstract: AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) are promising silicon sensor technologies for high-precision four-dimensional tracking. Position reconstruction in AC-LGADs relies on correlations among waveforms induced on multiple readout pads, where analytically solving the signal propagation becomes difficult, motivating data-based machine learning reconstruction. Existing machine learning approaches generally assume a fixed readout pad layout and predict one hit from an isolated, temporally aligned waveform window. These assumptions limit their flexibility across sensor designs and applicability to continuous readout where signal arrival times are not known in advance and multiple hits might overlap in the same waveforms. We introduce GeoRead, a spatial-temporal Transformer enabling multi-event continuous position prediction and uncertainty estimation. We incorporate relative pad positions into attention and produces time-resolved hit position estimates with predictive uncertainties. Time-jitter and additive event-mixing augmentations are used to train the model on temporally misaligned and overlapping waveforms synthesized from single-event measurements. Using four-channel transient-current-technique (TCT) data of a 500\mum-pitch AC-LGAD, GeoRead achieves median position errors of 5.8\mum within the convex hull of the readout-pad centers and 8.2\mum over the full scanned region at 190\volt. The model maintains comparable accuracy under temporal shifts and demonstrates time-resolved reconstruction of superposed events, without predefined per-event window. These results provide a basis for extending waveform-based position reconstruction toward continuous readout and flexible sensor geometries.
papers.reason: Applies spatial-temporal Transformers to continuous AC-LGAD silicon tracking reconstruction, which is adjacent to neutrino/collider detector instrumentation.

papers.title: Yang-Mills theories with scalar matter: a first foray using the Curci-Ferrari model
papers.abstract: The Curci-Ferrari (CF) model provides an efficient perturbative framework for describing several aspects of the infrared (IR) dynamics of Yang-Mills (YM) theories. We extend this framework to YM theories coupled with scalar matter and investigate its main properties, with particular emphasis on the one-loop two-point correlation functions of scalars, gluons, and ghosts. We analyze the renormalization group (RG) structure of the model, computing its beta functions and studying the corresponding RG flows for different scalar masses. We establish the existence of IR-safe trajectories along which perturbation theory remains under control and identify a novel fixed-point, while recovering the standard CF results in an appropriate limit. We then confront our results with lattice data through a simultaneous fit of the scalar, gluon, and ghost propagators, finding excellent agreement. Our results indicate that, within the approximations considered here, the CF framework gives a successful perturbative description of the IR regime of YM theories coupled with scalar matter.
papers.reason: Applies the Curci-Ferrari framework to Yang-Mills theories coupled with scalar matter to study IR properties and propagators.

papers.title: Dynamical gluon mass generation, the Schwinger mechanism, spontaneous symmetry breaking, and color confinement in the linear covariant gauges of QCD
papers.abstract: We critically re-examine the Kugo-Ojima (KO) scenario for color confinement and identify several inconsistencies and a crucial error in its derivation. Within the KO framework, under customary assumptions, we show that the BRST quartet structure incorporates a unique mechanism for dynamical gluon mass generation -- namely, the Schwinger mechanism, in the formulation developed by Aguilar, Binosi, Ferreira, and Papavassiliou (ABFP). We show that the Schwinger mechanism is a Higgs mechanism, in that it occurs together with the spontaneous breaking of the global gauge charge, as it should. The ABFP bound state is the associated (unphysical) composite Goldstone boson. The zero-momentum value of the gluon propagator evaluated in the Pinch Technique--Background-Field Method (PT-BFM) naturally emerges in the derivation, setting a Renormalization-Group invariant scale for mass generation and suggesting a new nonperturbative interpretation of the PT-BFM. BRST symmetry takes over the role of the broken symmetry, while the color symmetry of the spectrum remains unbroken. We obtain a unique, well-defined, unbroken, BRST-exact asymptotic color charge operator that realizes the confinement of color in the sense of the absence of colored asymptotic states from the BRST cohomology. Still within the KO framework, we take the first fundamental step towards a proof of the nonperturbative unitarity of the linear covariant gauges of QCD, and we discuss the experimental evidence in favor of the Schwinger mechanism. We lay down the foundations for a unified theory of gauge-boson mass generation in the linear covariant gauges of Yang-Mills theories.
papers.reason: Examines dynamical gluon mass generation, the Schwinger mechanism, and color confinement within linear covariant gauges of QCD.

papers.title: Interference effects in MSSM Higgs boson searches at low $tan\beta$: the $gg\to H\to WW, ZZ, hh$ and $gg \to A \to Zh$ channels
papers.abstract: The LHC limits on the heavy neutral Higgs bosons of the minimal supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model, which are particularly relevant at low values of the ratio of vacuum expectation values $\tan\beta$, have been obtained in the narrow-width approximation, without including the interference between the pure Higgs signal and the QCD background. We study the interference of the resonant heavy neutral CP-even $H$ and CP-odd $A$ boson contributions with the non-resonant gluon-fusion amplitudes in the processes $gg\to VV$ with $V=W,Z$, $gg \to hh$ and $gg\to Zh$ at low $\tan\beta$, $1\le \tan\beta \le 6$. We work at leading order but with the exact top-quark mass dependence, and with the longitudinal $VV$ and $Zh$ amplitudes obtained from the Goldstone-boson equivalence theorem that lead to loop form factors similar to those appearing in $gg\to hh$. The lineshapes in the four search channels are governed by a simple complex parameter $\kappa$, the ratio of the resonant to non-resonant amplitudes at the peak. Because the $H$ and $A$ bosons couple weakly to the considered final states, while being broadened by their decays to top quarks, $|\kappa|$ drops to values of a few for masses of $0.5$--$1$ TeV, even though the total widths remain at the percent level. The interference then increases the signal rates by up to tens of per cent, and distorts their lineshapes. For the present ATLAS (and presumably CMS) Run II exclusion limits, the net effect is nevertheless rather modest, except at the high-mass end of the $H\to hh$ contour, but it becomes important for the masses that will be probed at the high-luminosity LHC.
papers.reason: Analyzes interference between heavy MSSM Higgs resonances and non-resonant QCD backgrounds in gluon-fusion channels at low $\tan\beta$.

papers.title: Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data
papers.abstract: The reconstruction of the top-quark-pair ($t\bar{t}$) kinematics in the dilepton $t\bar{t}$ decay channel is challenging due to the presence of two undetected neutrinos. In this work, existing kinematic reconstruction methods used by the CMS Collaboration are studied using a Monte Carlo sample with $t\bar{t}$ events from CMS Open Data at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. An improved version of the loose kinematic reconstruction, LKRv2, is developed by imposing more stringent requirements on the jet-lepton pairing entering the reconstruction. A further modification, LKRv3, exploits the kinematic similarity between the dilepton and neutrino-pair systems and improves the resolution of the reconstructed $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass relative to the baseline LKR by $7\%$, with smaller improvements for the transverse momentum and rapidity of $t\bar{t}$. In addition, two machine-learning (ML) based approaches are developed using a residual multilayer perceptron and a conditional normalizing flow. Relative to LKRv3, they improve the resolution of the invariant mass, transverse momentum and rapidity by approximately $30\%$, $20\%$ and $15\%$, respectively. In particular, a resolution of 30 GeV is achieved for the reconstructed invariant mass of $t\bar{t}$ near the production threshold. A dedicated generator-level study and a generator-to-detector transfer test demonstrate that the ML approaches learn a genuine physics-driven correction to the $\nu\bar{\nu}$ approximation, rather than merely exploiting detector-specific effects. These results demonstrate the strong potential of ML-based approaches for improving the reconstruction of dilepton $t\bar{t}$ events, while identifying the neutrino-pair approximation as an important limitation on the achievable resolution.
papers.reason: Develops analytical and machine learning methods for top-quark pair kinematic reconstruction with missing neutrinos using CMS Open Data.

papers.title: Just CaloCHILL: fast hadronic shower generation in a learned latent space
papers.abstract: Calorimeter showers are the most expensive part of detector simulation, and highly granular calorimeters, in which a single hadronic shower leaves thousands of energy deposits, make them more expensive still. We present CaloCHILL (Calorimeter Hits In Learned Latents), a generative model that does not produce these deposits one by one: instead it generates a compact summary of the shower in a learned latent space and expands it to full resolution only at the end. The complete shower, including the arrival time of every hit, is built in three stages: a flow-matching model first sets the number of hits and the earliest hit time in each calorimeter layer, a mean-flow model then generates the latent summary, and the decompressor of a variational autoencoder turns it into the full point cloud, giving every hit its position, energy and time. Sparse attention along the shower axis keeps this compression affordable for showers with thousands of hits. On positive-pion showers in the calorimeter of the International Large Detector, a proposed detector for the FCC-ee, CaloCHILL reproduces the main shower observables, including their time structure. This new model is 600 times faster than its predecessor, while improving on all accuracy metrics considered.
papers.reason: Develops a generative model for fast hadronic shower simulation in high-granularity calorimeters, adjacent to neutrino event generation and detector simulation workflows.

papers.title: Higher Order Component Attribution via Learned Surrogates in High Energy Physics
papers.abstract: Experimental High Energy Physics (HEP) has adopted the transformer architecture for identification of jets, particularly the state-of-the-art Particle Transformer (ParT) which injects explicit information about particle correlations into the attention mechanism. While able to achieve state-of-the-art results in accuracy, interpretability to its effectiveness has been limited. In this paper we propose component attribution methods using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) that directly tie back to the physical descriptors of jets, to probe whether mechanisms such as Multi-Head Attention (MHA), or the ParT architecture, are able to learn these as discriminating features.
papers.reason: Uses Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for component attribution in jet physics transformers, relevant to machine learning workflows in high energy physics.

papers.title: Spiral momentum spectra and spin asymmetry in vacuum pair production driven by phase-modulated elliptically polarized electric fields
papers.abstract: We study vacuum electron--positron pair production in phase-modulated elliptically polarized electric fields using the quantum kinetic equations. We analyze how the modulation amplitude, frequency, ellipticity, and modulation form affect the spin-resolved momentum spectra and the spin asymmetry. Cosine-type modulation can deform ring-shaped momentum distributions into spiral patterns. This deformation depends nonmonotonically on the modulation amplitude and frequency and is most pronounced for circular polarization. In the transverse momentum plane, the spin-resolved yields favor the spin channel along the direction of field handedness. Reversing the field handedness would reverse the favored channel while leaving the total yield unchanged. Sine-type modulation preserves ring-shaped and mirror-symmetric spectra approximately, however, it leads to a stronger dependence of the spin asymmetry on the modulation amplitude than cosine-type modulation does. These results show that phase modulation and ellipticity can control the momentum spectra patterns in vacuum pair production. Moreover, phase modulation can also affect the degree of spin asymmetry.
papers.reason: Analyzes spin-resolved momentum spectra in vacuum electron-positron pair production driven by modulated electric fields.

papers.title: Parton density functions for future electron-positron colliders
papers.abstract: Precision QED radiative corrections are critical for the physics programs of future high-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders. We review the state-of-the-art QED parton density function (PDF) formalism for resumming collinear photon and pair emissions. Our numerical analysis of initial-state radiation (ISR) highlights the slow convergence of the perturbative series and the growing significance of pair production at higher orders. Finally, we emphasize the need to implement these theoretical refinements into modern Monte Carlo generators to meet the stringent precision demands of upcoming experimental measurements.
papers.reason: Reviews QED parton density functions and initial-state radiation resummation for future $e^+e^-$ colliders.

papers.title: Thermal Field Theory for General Equilibrium Density Matrices
papers.abstract: Thermal field theory (TFT) is the combination of statistical mechanics and relativistic quantum field theory. This (book) chapter provides a pedagogical introduction to (and a review of) TFT for general equilibrium density matrices, which allow arbitrary values not only of temperature and chemical potentials, but also of average angular momentum. A general technique to compute ensemble averages is illustrated. Path-integral methods are developed to study the partition function and the thermal Green's functions of general operators, with an arbitrary number of points, in all field theories of physical relevance.
papers.topic: Thermal Field Theory for General Ensembles
papers.reason: Provides a pedagogical review of thermal field theory for equilibrium density matrices with arbitrary temperatures, chemical potentials, and angular momentum.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of BDNK hydrodynamics: from heavy-ion collisions to astrophysics
papers.abstract: We present new developments in the mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of the causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamic theory by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK) in general spacetimes. We develop two independent flux-conservative algorithms for arbitrary 3+1-dimensional spacetime metrics. Both are hyperbolic, causal, and well-posed, pass convergence tests, and reproduce known results. The first uses a new first-order reduction with mathematically preserved constraints, whose numerical violations can be handled with cleaning fields (the resulting coupled system is proven hyperbolic and well-posed). The second uses a new mixed-order formulation, whose solutions are proven strictly equivalent to the original BDNK system, without cleaning fields. Our proofs rely on a new general theorem providing sufficient conditions for transforming a mixed-order system with arbitrary-order equations into a strictly hyperbolic system, strengthening a classical result by Choquet Bruhat for weak hyperbolicity. We introduce a new practical prescription for selecting admissible hydrodynamic frames for a broad class of equations of state, including nonconformal ones relevant to heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics. Our simulations capture viscous shock broadening and suppression of Kelvin--Helmholtz vortices, reproduce Bjorken and Gubser flows, and study departures from stationary ideal-fluid configurations in Michel accretion and rotating tori on fixed Schwarzschild and Kerr backgrounds. For heavy-ion collisions, we perform boost invariant simulations with a lattice-QCD-based equation of state and fluctuating TRENTo initial conditions, comparing BDNK with a minimal Israel--Stewart theory.
