The descriptions agree at small shear viscosity but can differ substantially at larger viscosities, particularly for early initialization with rapid longitudinal expansion.
papers.reason: Develops mathematical foundations and numerical algorithms for causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics.

papers.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
papers.abstract: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $\phi$ couples via the effective operator $\phi\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. Embedding $\phi$ as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory requires an anomaly coefficient $\gtrsim100$, implying a Landau pole for QCD. These tensions are relaxed for more strongly coupled dark gauge sectors.
papers.reason: Examines minimal warm inflation with gauge field couplings, touching upon early-universe particle physics but of peripheral interest.

papers.title: DarkMatterFM-Registry: A Machine-Readable Registry of Dark-Matter Models Extracted from the arXiv Literature
papers.abstract: To use a dark-matter model one needs to know what defines it, which observables it affects, which codes and likelihoods evaluate it, and under what assumptions a published bound applies. That information is scattered across tens of thousands of papers. We present DarkMatterFM-Registry, a machine-readable registry of dark-matter models extracted from arXiv full texts by a staged large-language-model (LLM) pipeline: 6,145 structured model cards, validated against a seven-file JSON Schema suite, ranked by expected value for observational follow-up, and enriched for the top ~2,000 with observables, constraints, and theory-to-observable routes. Schema checks pass 97.8% of cards, and an LLM-judged accuracy study on a stratified card sample finds 81% of section verdicts correct, 18% partially correct, and none hallucinated. As a first application we turn the registry into a priority-weighted roadmap of 25 concrete projects the community could build. The roadmap is built by judging every computational step of every enriched model's theory-to-observable routes as available, partial, or missing, and aggregating the resulting typed gaps weighted by model priority. We find that what blocks the most high-priority models is not missing theory but missing shared infrastructure: model files for existing relic-abundance solvers, a general non-cold Boltzmann-code framework, reusable indirect-detection likelihoods, and a Lyman-$\alpha$ forest likelihood for non-cold dark matter (the largest gap for structure-formation probes). The model cards, schemas, roadmap, and ranking are released making the project reproducible and the cards available for the community.
papers.reason: Presents a machine-readable registry and LLM pipeline for dark matter models, interesting from an AI/workflows perspective but not core physics.

papers.title: Andreev reflections and optimal truncation in the unitary Fermi droplet
papers.abstract: We study the unitary Fermi gas in an external trap in the double-scaling limit of large flavor number N and large charge Q at fixed Q/N. At leading order, the problem reduces to the spectral zeta function of a BdG operator in an inhomogeneous pairing background. The grand potential admits a gradient expansion with distinct bulk and edge sectors. We show that when the trap is harmonic, the bulk sector expansion terminates: beyond the first three terms every bulk contribution integrates to zero. This cancellation is general and follows from zeros of the Euler beta function computed in the Son-Wingate effective field theory, independent of the low-energy constants. The truncation persists for anisotropic traps in any odd dimension. All higher-order dependence for harmonic potentials is therefore carried by the droplet edge. For anharmonic traps, the asymptotic bulk series is factorially divergent. Using a heat-kernel WKB analysis, we show that its large-order growth, sign oscillations, and optimal truncation are fixed by complex periodic orbits of the BdG problem, which are analytic continuations of Andreev reflections. We numerically confirm the predicted Borel singularities for quartic and sextic traps.
papers.reason: Examines Andreev reflections and optimal truncation in unitary Fermi droplets, which is far from particle physics applications.

papers.title: NLO corrections to charged-current correlators near extremality: non-Abelian hydrodynamics meets AdS$_2$
papers.abstract: We analytically compute the longitudinal charged-current correlator in a near-extremal holographic plasma with quark and isospin chemical potentials, $\mu_q$ and $\mu_3$ respectively. To this end, we study fluctuations of gauge fields around a low-temperature AdS$_5$ Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole charged both under the quark number and the isospin. The result is obtained at next-to-leading order in a hydrodynamic expansion where apart from the temperature and isospin chemical potential, the frequency and momenta are small compared to the quark chemical potential, $\omega,k,T,\mu_3\ll\mu_q$. This approach captures the interplay between the hydrodynamic-like pole and the tower of infrared modes produced by the AdS$_2$ throat controlling the geometry of the black hole near extremality. At zero isospin chemical potential, the resulting quasinormal-mode formula reproduces the collision of the diffusive pole with the infrared spectrum, while the finite isospin chemical potential lifts this collision. The analytic spectrum agrees precisely with the full numerical results. The next-to-leading-order correlator also substantially improves the spectral function beyond the standard hydrodynamic regime $\omega,k,\mu_3\ll T$, extending the agreement with numerics to larger frequencies and momenta.
papers.reason: Computes holographic charged-current correlators near extremality, marginally relevant to transport properties in nuclear matter.

papers.title: Quasi-hydrodynamics beyond the conventional paradigm
papers.abstract: Quasi-hydrodynamics extends hydrodynamics by promoting slowly relaxing variables to additional degrees of freedom. For such a framework to be rigorously defined and parametrically controlled, the effective theory is usually assumed to retain all the slow modes of the underlying microscopic dynamics, which must be parametrically separated from the rest of the microscopic spectrum and typically arise from weakly broken symmetries. Here, we show that none of these assumptions is essential. Using the effective field theory of quasi-hydrodynamics recently derived from kinetic theory, we study three models that challenge the need for, respectively, parametric scale separation, retaining every slow mode, and a weakly broken symmetry. In all cases, the quasi-hydrodynamic expansion remains fully controlled and can be made arbitrarily accurate. This is possible because the applicability of quasi-hydrodynamics is determined not by the microscopic origin of the slow dynamics, but by the spectral properties of the kinetic operator on a suitably chosen Hilbert space.
papers.reason: Extends quasi-hydrodynamics beyond conventional assumptions using kinetic theory operator spectral properties.

papers.title: Towards a recursive construction of string scattering amplitudes
papers.abstract: We construct open superstring scattering amplitudes from three-point data using the Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten (BCFW) recursion and four-dimensional spinor helicity variables. We compute the contributions of selected leading and subleading Regge families to the color-ordered four-gluon amplitude by sewing their cubic couplings and summing over intermediate polarizations. The four-dimensional description makes helicity selection rules explicit and reduces the massive polarization sums to SU(2) little group contractions. The resulting residues are expressed in terms of Jacobi and Legendre polynomials, yielding explicit sums over mass levels. We construct a differential operator relating the two polynomial kernels, including their level-dependent normalizations. These results provide a concrete starting point for organizing the infinite intermediate-state sum and investigating whether relations among Regge families can support a recursive reconstruction of the full string amplitude.
papers.reason: Constructs string scattering amplitudes using BCFW recursion and spinor helicity variables.

papers.title: Nonstandard Dark Matter at Nonlinear Scales
papers.abstract: We investigate how two extensions of the standard $\Lambda$CDM scenario affect the evolution of the matter density and velocity divergence fields, from the linear regime to deeply nonlinear scales, using $N$-body simulations. We consider two well-motivated scenarios in which the canonical properties of dark matter (DM) are modified. In the first scenario, DM interacts with dark energy (DM--DE interaction). In the second scenario, we allow the DM equation-of-state parameter to deviate from the canonical pressureless limit, $w_{\rm DM}=0$. For the coupled DM--DE scenario, we find significant and scale-dependent deviations from $\Lambda$CDM of order $50$--$100\%$ in the matter power spectrum, persisting throughout the nonlinear regime, with the velocity divergence spectra providing complementary and partially independent sensitivity. For the $w_{\rm DM} \neq 0$ scenario, we find systematic but remarkably small deviations confined within $5\%$ across all scales probed. Our results identify which scales carry the greatest discriminatory power between these nonstandard scenarios and $\Lambda$CDM. We show that testing these models with current and forthcoming LSS surveys, through the analysis of density and/or velocity fields, will require a deeper theoretical understanding and accurate nonlinear modelling before robust constraints can be derived from observational data.
papers.reason: Investigates coupled dark matter and non-zero equation-of-state scenarios using N-body simulations, primarily cosmological structure formation.

papers.title: Density kernel and temporal quantum information probes in double-scaled SYK
papers.abstract: Entanglement is conventionally defined through a Hilbert space bipartition on a fixed time slice. Recent work has generalized this notion to multiple times through a non-Hermitian density kernel constructed from temporal correlation functions, encoding causal response, temporal non-classicality and quantum dynamics. We construct this kernel in the double-scaled Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (DSSYK) model using its exact chord Hilbert space formulation and study the resulting temporal information diagnostics. The direct sum structure of chord space naturally introduces a coarse-graining under which coherence between different chord sectors is removed. We show that the corresponding kernel measures quantify how information is dynamically transferred across subregions in the chord Hilbert space. We find that decreasing $\lambda$ enhances the propagation of temporal correlation across chord sectors, as well as the loss of memory within a fixed sector. This accelerated temporal dynamics in the small $\lambda$ limit coincides with the emergence of a semiclassical gravity description. Depending on the chord space partition, the probes exhibit either saturation, a growth followed by a decay, or temporary memory loss. The characteristic propagation time is nicely captured by a wavefront picture in Krylov space, with position-dependent hopping parameters that are determined by the DSSYK Lanczos coefficients. Finally, given the quantum sine-dilaton gravity description of DSSYK and its connections to de Sitter holography, our results provide a controlled setting for probing temporal quantum correlations across quantum and semiclassical gravitational regimes, and motivate a geometric interpretation of the density kernel.
papers.reason: Investigates temporal entanglement kernels in double-scaled SYK models, far from low-energy neutrino phenomenology.

papers.title: Simplicity of the three-point stress-tensor form factor beyond the planar limit
papers.abstract: We express the complete three-loop subleading-color finite remainder of the three-point stress-tensor-multiplet form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory as a permutation sum of a single $A_2$-type function. The non-product part of the seed is a combination of 35 weight-six generalized polylogarithms, while all lower-weight products and zeta-value terms belong to the same five-letter algebra. A bootstrap based on independently computed collinear data, branch-cut constraints and empirical final-entry relations determines both the symbol and the full function. The remaining function-level ambiguity is proportional to $\zeta_2$ times the two-loop planar remainder and is fixed by a single final-entry relation. The weight-three left coproduct factors of the planar and subleading-color results span the same space modulo products; at weight four, the subleading-color result contains four additional nonclassical directions. Through the established maximal-transcendentality correspondence, this compact representation also describes the weight-six subleading-color sector of Higgs-plus-three-gluon amplitudes in QCD. We also construct a four-loop candidate symbol space under a conjectural extension of the three-loop constraints.
papers.reason: Evaluates three-loop subleading-color form factors in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM and Higgs-plus-three-gluon amplitudes.

papers.title: Analogue Schwinger Pair Production in Acoustic Black Holes
papers.abstract: We show that an analogue Schwinger pair production can be realized in Reissner-Nordstr{\"o}m-like acoustic black holes constructed from a Bose-Einstein condensate subject to a synthetic vector potential. Upon Kaluza-Klein reduction of the five-dimensional acoustic geometry, the higher-dimensional phonon modes appear as effectively charged phonons in the resulting four-dimensional spacetime, in which the electric field experienced by the charged phonons arises from the component of the synthetic vector potential along the compactified direction. Then by appropriately choosing the background flow velocity and the synthetic vector potential, the reduced acoustic metric can take the form of a Reissner-Nordstr{\"o}m-like black hole. From this metric we obtain the mean number of spontaneously produced phonon pairs in both the extremal and near extremal cases, and show that in the extremal limit this mean number takes the form of the Schwinger formula. Moreover, charged-phonon pair production not only admits the same effective thermal interpretation as Schwinger pair production of real charged particles, but can also be interpreted as the analogue Hawking radiation and superradiance from the five-dimensional perspective. Finally, we make estimates of pair production using experimental parameters in Bose-Einstein condensate, providing theoretical guidance for future laboratory detection.
papers.reason: Examines acoustic black holes and analogue Schwinger pair production in Bose-Einstein condensates.

papers.title: Primordial or Post-Inflationary: Distinguishing the Origin of Scale-Dependent Features in the CMB
papers.abstract: Physics beyond the Standard Model, whether of primordial or post-inflationary origin, can leave scale-dependent signals in the anisotropies of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). In this work, we study how distinguishable these broad classes of signals are and quantify their level of degeneracy. In this initial investigation, for primordial features, we limit ourselves to those of the ``sharp'' and ``resonant'' kinds; for post-inflationary features, we consider two qualitatively distinct models: exotic energy injection, which deposits energy into the primordial plasma and modifies the global thermodynamic history, and early dark energy (EDE), which affects the CMB through the background expansion and gravitational perturbations. By studying representative examples, we find that while primordial features can leave oscillatory signatures in the CMB power spectrum with essentially arbitrary frequency and running, the post-inflationary models considered here produce qualitatively different patterns that cannot generically reproduce the characteristic running of primordial feature oscillations. We verify these findings first with a principal component analysis, and show using only the most significant principal components that there are no significant degeneracies between the primordial and post-inflationary features considered here, and secondly with a full likelihood analysis, which shows that the resulting posteriors do not change significantly when considering individual classes of models or combinations of primordial/post-inflationary features. While the two post-inflationary models probe distinct physical mechanisms and both are implemented in a simplified, phenomenological fashion, the methods used in this work can be generalized to include more realistic signals or other classes of signals.
papers.reason: Differentiates primordial versus post-inflationary CMB features, mostly standard cosmology.

papers.title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
papers.abstract: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale $c$, with splitting $\Delta(c)\propto1/c$. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the $(4+\epsilon)$-dimensional $O(N)$ model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of $N$ through $N=4$ has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.
papers.reason: Mathematical analysis of Conley index theory applied to expanding plasma models, which is outside core neutrino interests.

papers.title: Primordial non-Gaussianity as a large-scale cosmic-web bias
papers.abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity is a unique probe of the physics of inflation, but its large-scale-structure signature is difficult to measure because it appears on the largest, most cosmic-variance-limited modes. The standard view of local-type primordial non-Gaussianity is isotropic: it induces a scale-dependent correction to tracer bias, $\Delta b(k)\propto f_{\rm NL}k^{-2}$, on large scales. Here we show that the same large-scale response can be reformulated as an anisotropic, nonlocal environmental-bias effect. Motivated by the spectral cosmic-web hierarchy of Kitaura and Sinigaglia, we define a Hessian field $\mathcal{H}_{ij}(\bf{x})\equiv\partial_i\partial_j\nabla^{-4}\delta(\bf{x})$, whose trace obeys $\mathrm{Tr}\mathcal{H}=\nabla^{-2}\delta$ and therefore carries the same $k^{-2}$ enhancement that appears in the Dalal et al. scale-dependent-bias term. Diagonalizing $\mathcal{H}_{ij}$ defines four large-scale web environments, analogous to knots, filaments, sheets, and voids, although operating on scales much larger than the conventional nonlinear cosmic web. We assign one weight to each environment and test the construction with the AbacusPNG suite of local-PNG $N$-body simulations, using $f_{\rm NL}=\{-100,-30,30,100\}$. We show that these four weights reproduce the large-scale $k^{-2}$ rise of the tracer bias. We further show that existing halo catalogs without PNG can be post-processed to imprint an effective $f_{\rm NL}$ signature. Beyond mock generation, the resulting cosmic-web response motivates an observational statistic based on changes in tracer occupation of large-scale environments relative to a matched Gaussian reference, complementary to the conventional low-$k$ power spectrum.
papers.reason: Re-formulates primordial non-Gaussianity as a large-scale cosmic-web environmental bias.

papers.title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black-hole X-ray binaries show nonlinear coupling with broadband variability, producing characteristic ridge, hypotenuse, and web-like structures in the bicoherence. However, the origin of these structures remains unclear. We develop a mathematical model in which a modulator phase-locked to the QPO acts multiplicatively on the underlying variability. The resulting frequency mixing naturally produces both the ridge and hypotenuse associated with the fundamental QPO, as two parts of the same modulation-induced bispectral structure, and the same mechanism extends to the second harmonic. The model further predicts opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. We test these predictions using NICER observations of Swift~J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI~J1820$+$070. The bispectral maps show QPO-related ridge--hypotenuse structures broadly consistent with the model, with qualitatively opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. In particular, the biphase map provides a complementary diagnostic that reveals weak coupling structures that are difficult to identify from the bicoherence alone. We also compare the measured bispectral modulus with the predictions for isolated ridges and hypotenuses. These predictions broadly reproduce the observed frequency dependence, while localized deviations remain near the fundamental-QPO and second-harmonic frequencies, where different bispectral structures overlap. Our results provide a simple mathematical framework in which the web-like pattern in the bispectrum could arise naturally from multiplicative coupling between a QPO-phase-locked modulator and the underlying variability.
papers.reason: Astrophysical timing analysis of quasi-periodic oscillations in black hole X-ray binaries.

papers.title: Particle production from noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole
papers.abstract: By considering a massless Klein-Gordon field and the moving mirror model, we calculate particle production for a noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole sourced by smeared distributions of mass and charge. We show that noncommutative truncated trajectories diminish the emission spectrum at large frequencies, due to noncommutative effects on the external surface gravity of the black hole, in sharp contrast with the spectrum of a classical Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole.
papers.reason: Calculates particle production from noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordström black holes.

papers.title: Explicit Symmetry Breaking in Non-Abelian Scalar Theories and One-Loop Renormalization
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian gauge theories coupled to scalar fields are fundamental in particle physics, yet they often face high-energy instabilities. In this work, we start by analyzing the classical $SU(2)$ complex scalar model, mapping the scalar multiplet into a real $SO(2N)$ representation to formalize its generalization to $SU(N)$. Within this classical setup, we introduce an explicit gauge symmetry breaking exclusively in the scalar sector by splitting the mass parameters and quartic self-coupling constants. Moving to the quantum level, we employ the background field method and the Schwinger-DeWitt technique to compute the exact one-loop divergences, explicitly demonstrating the renormalizability of the broken theory. Finally, we derive the Renormalization Group equations and analyze the fixed points of the flow. It is shown that this explicit symmetry breaking asymptotically destabilizes the theory, driving the scalar couplings away from the origin and inevitably leading to a Landau pole.
authors: Lucas Ducastelo de C. C. Lima
papers.reason: Formal study of explicit gauge symmetry breaking in non-Abelian scalar theories lacks connection to neutrino or EFT phenomenology.

papers.title: Discreetly Conformal: Higher-Order Chiral Scalars and the Discrete Series
papers.abstract: With its constant shift symmetry gauged, a massless scalar on two-dimensional flat space defines a conformal field theory whose classical phase space is equivalent to that of a chiral and an anti-chiral Floreanini--Jackiw scalar. We show that this picture generalizes: After gauging a larger set of the shift symmetries of the massless scalar field, it decomposes into a pair of generalized chiral and anti-chiral scalars, described by actions with higher-order spatial derivatives. We spell out their physical and gauge symmetries, and show how these give rise to the hidden conformal symmetry of the scalar with gauged shift symmetries. This lifts to de Sitter space, where we find that the discrete series scalars also decompose into these generalized chiral scalars, providing an explanation for their hidden conformal symmetry.
papers.reason: Purely formal conformal field theory study of generalized chiral scalars.

papers.title: Analytic Bounds on Conformal Defect Spectra
papers.abstract: Conformal defects describe impurities and boundaries at criticality. Their stability depends on the scaling dimensions of operators localized on the defects, but these dimensions are often difficult to determine. We derive analytic upper bounds on the lowest nonvacuum scaling dimension using only two defect entropies and the dimension of a defect-changing operator. The bounds identify when relevant operators must appear on the defect with larger defect entropy. They follow from the conformal bootstrap of four-point functions of defect-changing operators and apply to unitary conformal line defects and to conformal boundaries in two-dimensional CFTs. The Ising and Potts models provide exact checks. In three-dimensional $O(N)$ models, we apply the bounds to direct sums of pinning field defects with symmetry-related orientations. Data from a single such defect exclude stable impurity order with three or more orientations in $O(2)$ and $O(3)$, or four or more in $O(4)$, for any geometry of the orientations, and require a relevant domain-wall operator between individually stable pinning field defects at every nonzero relative angle up to $120^\circ$ in $O(3)$ and up to $109.47^\circ$ in $O(4)$. A direct fuzzy-sphere computation of the lowest domain-wall dimension at different relative angles for $N=2,3,4$ is consistent with these bounds and indicates that, within this class of impurities, only two-state order remains a candidate for stable order in $O(3)$ and $O(4)$, while none survives in $O(2)$. A separate application to AdS/BCFT shows that, at fixed unequal brane tensions, a light boundary-condition-changing operator requires additional light primaries on the boundary with larger boundary entropy.
papers.reason: Derives analytic bounds on conformal defect spectra within formal CFTs.

papers.title: Fermionic Kaluza-Klein Reductions
papers.abstract: We work out the Kaluza--Klein (KK) compactification on a general product spacetime for free spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 fields in arbitrary dimension. The analysis is performed at the level of the action, and the resulting lower-dimensional theory describes infinite towers of massive particles whose masses are related to the eigenvalues of the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators on the internal space. A Hodge-like decomposition is used to write down a KK ansatz for spin-3/2 fields, and the fate of gauge invariance is discussed.
papers.reason: Performs Kaluza-Klein compactifications for free spin-1/2 and 3/2 fields in higher dimensions.

papers.title: AdS to dS Flows Dual to Pseudo-Hermitian Theories
papers.abstract: We construct generalizations of ''centaur" geometries in more than two dimensions as solutions of Einstein gravity coupled to a ghost scalar. The solutions interpolate between asymptotically anti-de Sitter and asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes, with the two asymptotic regions separated by a horizon. A holographic interpretation is that they are dual to pseudo-Hermitian theories obtained from the continuation of real couplings and operators to purely imaginary values. One family of solutions is obtained from a supergravity theory that is a consistent truncation with a known embedding in string theory. We study the thermodynamic and linear stability of the solutions, and determine the uplift of the supergravity solutions to eleven dimensions.
papers.reason: Constructs holographic solutions interpolating between AdS and dS for pseudo-Hermitian theories.

papers.title: Reflecting Baths and Black Hole Interior Islands in JT Gravity
papers.abstract: We study the evolution of entanglement entropy within the island prescription in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to finite non-gravitating baths bounded by reflecting walls. For free massless Dirac matter, we study the evolution of entanglement entropy, explicitly accounting for correlations induced by the reflecting boundaries. For sufficiently short baths, the no-island entropy saturates below the thermodynamic black hole entropy, avoiding the usual information paradox associated with its unbounded growth. For larger baths, reflected correlations drive the exterior quantum extremal surface toward the future horizon, leading to a temporary disappearance of the the near-horizon exterior island branch. We find that this branch first appears at a scrambling-like scale, and it reappears at a time that is proportional to the size of the bath. We extend the extremization across the horizon using regular Kruskal coordinates and identify real quantum extremal surfaces in the black hole interior. We show that, in the parameter regime studied, interior island configurations provide the dominant contribution to the radiation entropy during the exterior disappearance time interval, resolving the reappearance of the information paradox in an exterior-only description.
papers.reason: Studies entanglement entropy and island prescriptions in JT gravity.

papers.title: A Song of Spice and Ice: A diagonal dual to dS$_3$ & its Galilean flat space limit
papers.abstract: We propose a diagonal CFT dual to asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes in three dimensions (3d), constructed from the holomorphic part of the CFT dual at the future boundary and the antiholomorphic part of the CFT dual at the past boundary, in part inspired by an antipodal map between the two CFT copies. This gives equal and opposite imaginary central charges for the holomorphic and antiholomorphic sectors. The corresponding diagonal holographic energy-momentum tensor expectation values are constructed from the Wavefunction at the future boundary and its conjugate. This enables a recovery of the entropy of $dS_3$, as well as a family of complex Kerr $dS_3$ spacetimes with two real horizons, by a Cardy formula. We then explore the flatspace limit of our dS construction. With the central charges as above, the flatspace limit naturally induces a Galilean contraction on the dual diagonal 2d CFT, in contrast to the more familiar Carrollian limit when 3d Asymptotically Flat Spacetime (AFS) is approached from $AdS_3$. The corresponding limit for the complex Kerr family above leaves the inner horizon intact, resulting in flat space complex black holes ($\mathbb{C}$BH) that are closely related to flat space cosmologies which arise from BTZ black holes in AdS$_3$. We recover the entropy of these $\mathbb{C}$BHs by the BMS-Cardy formula.
papers.reason: Explores holographic duals for three-dimensional de Sitter spaces.

papers.title: Dressed AdS$_4$ black holes in M-theory from the 3d superconformal index
papers.abstract: The superconformal index of 4d $\mathcal N\,{=}\,4$ SYM has been shown to exhibit a rich phase structure, whose holographic interpretation in AdS$_5$ involves (dual-)dressed black holes, gray galaxies, and graviton gas contributions. Here we extend the analysis to 3d CFTs, focusing on ABJM theory and the $\mathcal N=4$ ADHM theory. We study the microcanonical superconformal index with two independent charges at finite $N$ and obtain exact signed state degeneracies up to large charges. The results exhibit the black hole physics expected to emerge at large-$N$, including isolated black holes and black holes dressed by additional matter.
papers.reason: Analyzes superconformal indices and holographic black holes in M-theory.

papers.title: Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
papers.abstract: We formulate the scalar and form-field sector of type IIB supergravity as an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary. Unlike the pseudo-action, it is a genuine action principle with manifest global $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry. The IIB fields arise as edge modes: a boundary term breaks the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, so the axion-dilaton parametrizes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(2)$, and the boundary field equations give the duality relations, including $F_5$ self-duality. As the action never refers to the axion-dilaton directly, S-duality monodromies become holonomies of a flat connection.
papers.reason: Formulates type IIB supergravity scalar and form fields via topological field theory.

papers.title: AdS${}_3$/BCFT${}_2$ correspondence and 't Hooft anomaly of U(1) symmetry
papers.abstract: We investigate how a U(1) 't Hooft anomaly obstructs symmetry-preserving boundary conditions from the perspective of the AdS${}_3$/BCFT${}_2$ correspondence. By considering a U(1) Maxwell--Chern--Simons system in the bulk spacetime, we show that the BCFT current is not conserved at the boundary. We also derive the general solution for the gauge field in AdS${}_2$ slicing.
papers.reason: Investigates U(1) 't Hooft anomalies and boundary conditions in AdS3/BCFT2.

papers.title: Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space
papers.abstract: The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer from infrared divergences
papers.reason: Proposes an inductive process replacing Feynman diagrams to avoid infrared divergences in QED.

papers.title: Carrollian minimal massive gravity and the fate of third-way consistency
papers.abstract: We construct the Carrollian limit of minimal massive gravity. The limit is singular for the algebra and regular for the Chern-Simons-like data. The one divergent bracket points along the null direction of the contracted bilinear form. The Lagrangian is therefore finite while the brackets are not. The contracted curvature still obeys a cubic closure condition, forced on shell rather than identically. The third-way coupling itself, however, is removable. For generic parameters an invertible redefinition of the auxiliary field and the boost connection takes it to Carrollian topologically massive gravity up to a boundary term. The same redefinition fails before the limit. We solve for an anti-de Sitter vacuum and a Carrollian black hole, whose rotation parameter leaves the frame and survives only in the boost connection. The degenerate vector flavor metric obstructs the standard charge formula, which we replace by a canonical one. The boundary charges, obtained in two independent ways, carry no trace of the deformation. A Dirac analysis gives nine first-class constraints and no local degrees of freedom on any background. The massive graviton is removed. The asymptotic symmetry algebra is bms_3, with central charges carried by the Einstein and Lorentz-Chern-Simons terms. The black hole has two sets of thermodynamic data, each with its own first law. One obeys the Bekenstein-Hawking area law, the other keeps the Chern-Simons entropy.
papers.reason: Constructs Carrollian limits of minimal massive gravity and studies its boundary charges.

papers.title: Pfaffian sensitivity to temporal deformations of an N=5 background in the Lorentzian IIB matrix model
papers.abstract: How spacetime dimensionality and anisotropy emerge from matrix degrees of freedom is a central question in the IIB matrix model. Our previous work constructed a family of constrained classical solutions at $N=5$, including a reference configuration with vanishing temporal extent and a pre-existing $3+6$ spatial hierarchy. Here we examine how the fermionic Pfaffian responds to temporal-matrix deformations of this configuration. The background geometry determines a distinguished real two-plane of temporal deformations. Numerical analysis of the full fermionic operator shows that the sensitivity of its lowest positive-eigenvalue doublet is strongly concentrated in this plane and dominates the first-order Pfaffian response. Under stated reflection-covariance and nonsingularity conditions, the other local one-loop contributions cancel at first order when combined, so the gradients of the logarithmic magnitudes of the total local one-loop weight and the Pfaffian agree. We prescribe a temporal deformation along the projection of this gradient onto the two-plane and determine the remaining matrix components by conditional classical stationarity. The existing spatial hierarchy is modestly strengthened at quadratic order, while the spectrum changes little at the small amplitude considered. This quadratic response is independent of orientation within the plane, although the first-order Pfaffian response distinguishes such orientations. These results connect background geometry, fermionic spectral sensitivity, and conditional classical spatial anisotropy.
papers.reason: Analyzes fermionic Pfaffians and temporal matrix deformations in the Lorentzian IIB matrix model.

papers.title: Null Strings Gauged, Reloaded and Quantized, II: Null Strings on Flat Backgorund Have Discrete Spectrum
papers.abstract: We continue our study of the quantization of null strings, strings with Carrollian worldsheets described by an action with two-dimensional (2d) diffeomorphisms, Weyl and Carroll-Weyl scaling as gauge symmetry. We perform light cone gauge quantization of the null strings on flat space background within Schr\"odinger representation, initiated in arXiv:2607.02970. We show, within the regular separated Schr\"odinger sector, that bosonic null strings on a flat background have no critical dimensions, have discrete, nonnegative mass-squared levels and are hence free of tachyonic modes.
papers.reason: Performs light-cone gauge quantization of null strings on flat backgrounds.

papers.title: The instanton sum in two-dimensional self-dual models
papers.abstract: This paper considers the self-dual $CP^{N-1}$ model in two dimensions, which is defined by restricting the path integral of the ordinary two-dimensional $CP^{N-1}$ model to holomorphic configurations. We find that the instanton measure is one-loop exact and agrees with the one-loop instanton measure in the ordinary model. For the $N=2$ case, the instanton gas admits a description in terms of free massive Dirac fermions. Nevertheless, we find that the self-dual model is gapless. We also comment on the $\theta$ dependence.
papers.reason: Studies instanton measures and self-duality in two-dimensional $CP^{N-1}$ models.

papers.title: Remark on residual solutions in the $KBc$ algebra
papers.abstract: In this paper we study residual solutions of open bosonic string field theory in the $KBc$ algebra with the auxiliary identities $(\partial^mc)^2=0$ of the ghost field. These solutions are not covered by the classification based on the defining relations alone. We show that the operator which controls the cohomology on the residual family depends only on $s=\gamma_1+\gamma_2$. At positive level $n$, cohomology can appear only on the lines $s=\pm n$. We compute it through level four and find one class at every point of each line $s=-3$ and $s=-4$. These classes give exact polynomial deformations of the residual family. At level six on $s=-6$, the cohomology instead vanishes generically and has dimension two at $(-1,-5)$ and $(-5,-1)$. We also compute the failure of the standard generator redefinition to preserve the auxiliary identities, and discuss the regularization of an explicit residual solution.
papers.reason: Studies residual solutions and cohomologies in string field theory's $KBc$ algebra.

papers.title: 5d $\mathbb{Z}_2$ S-folds and Seiberg--Witten curves
papers.abstract: We compute the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ S-folds of five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ rank-1 superconformal field theories. Two complementary constructions are presented. First, we implement the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ action by identifying pairs of points on the original curve, thereby mapping them to a single point on the S-folded curve. Second, motivated by arXiv:2112.14550, we tune mass parameters to special values, corresponding to the insertion of $D_4$ 7-branes. As a nontrivial consistency check, we show that the two Seiberg--Witten curves agree with each other when expressed in the Weierstrass normal form.
papers.reason: Computes Seiberg-Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ S-folds of 5D SCFTs.

papers.title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
papers.abstract: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.
papers.reason: Mathematical construction of quantum Casimirs and reflection equations.

papers.title: Equatorial Periodic Orbits and Gravitational Wave Signatures in Weyl Geometric Gravity Black Holes
papers.abstract: Weyl geometric gravity theory is a gravitational theory with Lagrangian density constructed from the square of the Weyl curvature scalar and the strength of the Weyl vector. The theory can be reformulated as a scalar - vector - tensor theory in the Riemann geometry by introducing an auxiliary scalar field, in the presence of a non - minimal coupling between the Ricci scalar and the scalar field. Assuming that the Weyl vector has only a radial component, an exact spherically symmetric black hole type solution of the field equations in the vacuum can be obtained. The solution depends on three arbitrary integration constants. As compared to the case of the Schwarzschild black hole, the Weyl geometric gravity black hole solution contains two new terms, linear and quadratic, in the radial coordinate. It is the main goal of the present work to investigate astrophysical properties of the Weyl geometric black holes by considering the behavior of the timelike geodesics, which allows to explore how the geometric nonmetricity influences the strong-field dynamics of massive test particles as well as the topological structure of the periodic orbits. The resulting gravitational wave emission in extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) systems is also considered. Our results show that the presence of nonmetricity in Weyl geometric gravity leaves distinct and measurable signatures on both the orbital topology and the emitted gravitational waveforms of compact EMRI systems. These unique temporal and amplitude modulations provide a promising observational avenue for testing the presence of nonmetricity on cosmic scales.
papers.reason: Astrophysical properties and orbits in alternative gravity black holes.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole: Linear stability and strong cosmic censorship conjecture
papers.abstract: We present an alternative formulation of coupled gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black holes, yielding decoupled radial and angular equations with a well-defined $\Lambda\rightarrow 0$ limit. We compute the quasinormal mode spectra using spectral and direct integration methods, finding excellent agreement. All of these modes are consistent with the linear stability of the Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole. We investigate the photon sphere and near-extremal modes, revealing a non-trivial interplay between rotation and electric charge. We further explore the implications for the strong cosmic censorship conjecture and find that the photon sphere modes predominantly determine its validity within the parameter space considered. While increasing the rotation of the black hole generally favours the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, increasing the electric charge can promote its violation. We also find that the region of parameter space exhibiting a violation of the conjecture is comparatively smaller for gravitational perturbations than for electromagnetic perturbations. These results highlight the important role of rotation, electric charge, and the nature of perturbations in determining the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in Kerr--Newman--de Sitter spacetimes.
papers.reason: General relativity study of black hole quasinormal modes and cosmic censorship.

papers.title: Generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics from gravitational perturbations of near-extremal Kerr
papers.abstract: We derive the generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics of near-extremal Kerr directly from four-dimensional gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometry. We construct two families of exact linear perturbations of the near-NHEK background: a non-normalizable mode that deforms the asymptotic boundary, and a normalizable mode supported near the horizon. Both perturbations are smooth solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations reduced to the Jackiw--Teitelboim equation for the dual scalar, without conical singularities. We study their asymptotic symmetries and show that they generate an algebra of time reparametrizations; requiring the gauge parameters to depend on the Schwarzian mode, the isometry condition selects the stationary KdV hierarchy. The same hierarchy is independently enforced by the vacuum Einstein equations on the perturbation coefficient. In the Euclidean regime, we evaluate the Hamiltonian action and show that each mode independently generates a tower of odd-power corrections to the near-extremal entropy.
papers.reason: Formal gravitational perturbations and near-extremal Kerr thermodynamics.

papers.title: The K\"ahler Stability Wall in Perturbative Brane--Antibrane Inflation
papers.abstract: Perturbative brane--antibrane inflation requires the physical K\"ahler volume to remain stabilized while the anti-D3 sector supplies the inflationary energy. This paper shows that this requirement imposes an exact analytic boundary on the allowed anti-D3 tension. In the leading nilpotent effective theory, the K\"ahler minimum and the decompactification barrier disappear through a saddle-node degeneration determined by \(U_\sigma=U_{\sigma\sigma}=0\). The positive-tension branch of this boundary is solved in closed form and uniformized by a single real parameter. The same solution fixes the local scaling of the K\"ahler mass, barrier height, and canonical distance to the endpoint. Integrating out the volume modulus reveals a Schur-complement singularity, showing that the adiabatic single-field description fails at the same boundary unless the inflaton--volume mixing is suppressed. The result is then translated into necessary flux-arithmetic filters involving the warped throat, D3 tadpole, conifold control, scalar normalization, and the full K\"ahler-sector mass matrix. Numerical tests verify the critical locus, the saddle-node scaling laws, and the resulting sparse throat-flux filtration. These conditions are necessary for compact realizations; no compact vacuum is asserted without the corresponding global and Wilsonian control checks.
papers.reason: String theory cosmology has no relevance to neutrino interaction physics or precision electroweak probes.

papers.title: Edge dynamics of covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons
papers.abstract: We study the covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons in 2+1 dimensions in the presence of a planar boundary. The differential generator associated with the scalar gauge symmetry singles out a single scalar Ward combination of the functional field equations. Its zeroth and first normal moments give two integrated boundary identities. The zeroth moment yields a traceless rank-two current obeying a fractonic double-divergence conservation law and a higher-rank Kac-Moody algebra. The first moment makes the normal-tangential field $w_i=h_{2i}$ explicit and yields an ordinarily conserved vector current with a standard $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra. Functional differentiation also produces a mixed equal-time bulk-boundary commutator between $w_1$ and $h_{11}$: it is non-vanishing at finite normal distance and vanishes in the intrinsic boundary limit. The equal-time commutators of the boundary current with the spatial components of the gauge-invariant field strength vanish, so microcausality is satisfied; when the boundary parameters are such that the two boundary sectors decouple, its retarded response vanishes at all times. Locally, the boundary constraints are solved by $w_i=\partial_i\chi$ and $h_{ij}=\partial_i\partial_j\xi+\eta_{ij}\phi$. When the boundary parameters are such that the two sectors decouple, the induced action is the direct sum of a chiral boson in the $w_i$ sector and a higher-rank sector in which $\phi$ is auxiliary and $\psi=\partial_1\xi$ is the propagating field. The latter has a non-chiral Luttinger description on its positive-energy branch and admits a chiral reduction. The boundary conditions determine the velocity and positivity branch of the $w_i$ mode, while the compatibility analysis in the $h_{ij}$ sector selects the positive-energy branch. On the positive-energy branch the two chiral modes co-propagate with orientation opposite to the sign of $\kappa$.
papers.reason: (keyword-ranked)

papers.title: The Double Copy of the Doubly Spinning Black Ring
papers.abstract: We establish an exact curved-background Weyl double copy for the doubly spinning Pomeransky--Sen'kov black ring. Its full Weyl tensor is a quadratic form in two source-free Maxwell fields: one generated by the stationary Killing vector, the other a flux-carrying magnetic field obtained by linearizing the dipole-ring gauge potential about its vacuum limit. The mixed Maxwell bilinear is essential: no spacetime-independent real or complex change of field basis removes it. We identify the inverse $S_{IJ}$ of the Weyl coefficient matrix as a matrix zeroth copy. The same matrix arises independently from a weighted limit of the inner products of two Killing vectors in a six-dimensional Ricci-flat parent and satisfies $\Box_g S_{IJ}=-\tfrac12 F_{I\,ab}F_J{}^{ab}$. The singly spinning limit recovers the diagonal two-field Weyl double copy of the Emparan--Reall ring.
papers.reason: Purely formal gravitational double-copy research in general relativity and string theory, which is irrelevant to neutrino physics.

papers.title: On Superconformal Index Degenerations and Half-Indices in S-Confining Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We study the $p \rightarrow 0$ limit of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal indices and its relation to half-indices of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories. At the level of special functions, this limit reduces elliptic hypergeometric integrals to basic hypergeometric integrals. The scaling of the flavor fugacities determines the Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions of the chiral multiplets. The gauge multiplet has Neumann boundary conditions. We apply this prescription to s-confining theories with gauge groups $SU(2)$, $USp(2N)$, $G_2$, and $SU(N)$, and recover the half-index identities of several boundary confining dualities, expressed through the Nassrallah-Rahman and Gustafson integrals. For $SU(N)$ with a rank-two antisymmetric chiral, four fundamentals and $N$ antifundamentals, we obtain an analytic proof of the half-index identities proposed by Okazaki and Smith for all $N \geq 5$.
papers.reason: Formal supersymmetric gauge theory and special functions without any low-energy or neutrino applications.

papers.title: 99.9...% of the SU(2) BFSS ground state
papers.abstract: We solve for the ground-state wavefunction of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz method to an auxiliary operator $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$. We show that this operator agrees with the Hamiltonian on the ground-state subspace and has a spectral gap. For SU(2) specifically, the representation theory of the singlet sector gives an astronomical reduction in the number of degrees of freedom. This allows us to construct an efficient variational basis whose inner products we compute exactly. We demonstrate the method by computing a state that satisfies rigorous bounds on its energy $E\,g_{\mathrm{YM}}^{-2/3}\leq 4.18\times10^{-8}$ and ground-subspace overlap $\|P_{\ker H}\psi\|^2\geq 0.999997$. We compute ground-state moments with high precision, finding values consistent with the bounds from our matrix bootstrap. Additionally, the state accurately reproduces both the exponent and coefficient of the asymptotic radial probability density predicted by the three-graviton amplitude.
papers.reason: Matrix model wavefunctions and supersymmetric quantum mechanics are outside the scope of neutrino and precision physics.

papers.title: Existence of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap
papers.abstract: Extremal solutions and functionals play an important role in the conformal bootstrap. These are the solutions that saturate unitarity bounds, and the dual functionals that encode the optimal bounds. While they have fundamental theoretical implications, their existence has not been rigorously established. This is particularly subtle in the setting of the full infinite-dimensional bootstrap, i.e. the limit of zero numerical truncation. In this article, we prove that extremal solutions exist for OPE maximisation problems in 1d CFT. These are a large class of generically interacting, unitary, exact solutions of the crossing equation that maximise an OPE coefficient. We also prove that these problems have 'zero duality gap', meaning there exist functionals arbitrarily close to extremality. Our approach is to formulate the bootstrap as a convex optimisation problem in a Hilbert space and apply the Fenchel-Rockafellar theorem.
papers.reason: Mathematical proof of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap, unrelated to the reader's interests.
